Life Cycle of Cultural Tourism Performance
Based on the years following the performance’s premier, the operation stage can be further
divided into four phases: the incubation phase, the growth phase, the maturity phase and the
innovation and enhancement phase. These phases constitute the entire lifecycle of a cultural tourism
performance project.
The incubation phase: This phase typically occurs within the first one to two years after the
cultural tourism performance is launched. At this time, the project has just been introduced to the
market and has not yet been widely recognised by the audience. Meanwhile, the supporting products
and services are not fully established, and the market demand cannot be guaranteed. Cultural tourism
performance companies often engage in marketing activities and other market initiatives to gradually
cultivate the market through strategic planning.
The growth phase: This phase typically occurs around five years after the cultural tourism
performance is launched. The project has gradually gained preliminary market acceptance, and its
visibility and number of audience attendance steadily increases, with the emergence of revisiting
audience. The supporting products and services are also improving. Cultural tourism performance
companies continuously make adjustments and optimisations to their products based on market
feedbacks, and simultaneously collaborate with surrounding tourism attractions to carry out relevant
promotional activities, further enhancing the market awareness of the cultural tourism performance.
− 98 −

=== PAGE 107 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
The maturity phase: This phase typically occurs around 10 years after the cultural tourism
performance is launched. The project has been widely accepted by the market and enjoys a high level
of brand awareness and good reputation. Tourists have clear expectations for the performance. Box
office receipts have peaked and are trending towards stability. Supporting products and services are
already well-established. Meanwhile, cultural tourism performance companies typically adopt brand
strategies, strengthen the construction and operation of both online and offline channels, extend a
series of experiential activities, and enhance the cooperation with surrounding tourism spots, hotels
and travel agencies. These measures aim to clarify the brand positioning and enhance its brand
influence, thereby strengthening its risk resistance capabilities.
The innovation and enhancement phase: This phase typically occurs around 15 years after the
cultural tourism performance is launched. With the continuous introduction of new cultural tourism
performances in the market, consumer interests are shifting. Therefore, cultural tourism performance
companies need to regularly adjust and optimise the performance to maintain its high quality and
attractiveness. For example, they can expand into new themes or storylines to enrich the performance
content, launch a series of performances based on different seasons or festivals to attract audience to
watch multiple times, and experiment with new performance forms or artistic elements to bring
audiences an entirely new visual and auditory experience. At the same time, companies will increase
their promotional efforts, utilising emerging marketing methods such as social media and influencer
marketing, to continuously maintain the brand’s influence and coverage.
Overall, cultural tourism performances, through continuous enhancement and innovation, as well
as adaptations such as seasonal editions, are able to extend their life cycles. Currently, the top 5% of
cultural tourism performance projects in terms of revenue in the industry have all been launched for
more than a decade. China’s cultural tourism performance industry can be traced back to 1982 with
the debut of “Imitation of Tang Music and Dance”, marking a 43-year history to the end of 2024.
“Songcheng Eternal Love”, a prominent production in the theme park performance, has been in
operation for almost 30 years since its launch. As a pioneering work in tourism scenery performance
industry of China, “Impression — Liu Sanjie” has also been staged for 21 years. In the realm of stage
play, “Thunderstorm”, which is first performed in 1934, stands as one of the longest-running and most
influential Chinese plays. It has evolved into a classic intellectual property (IP) and continues to tour
on a regular basis. In terms of overseas market, the opera performance “Cats” and “The Phantom of
the Opera”, which was premiered in 1981 and 1986 respectively, have since maintained performance
histories of 44 and 39 years, respectively. Additionally, Broadway itself boasts a theatrical heritage
dating back to the early 19th century, with over 200 years of continuous development.
Cultural Tourism Performance Market in China and Fujian Province
As national disposable income continues to rise, people have more funds available for
consumption that is beyond basic living needs. In terms of consumption concepts, people are
increasingly focused on spiritual satisfaction and personalised experiences, with their consumption
preferences shifting from traditional materials to high-quality and diversified services. Specifically in
the context of tourism sector. The increase in disposable income enables tourists to afford more
expensive tourism products and also makes them more willing to invest time and money in gaining
a deep understanding of the cultural connotations behind the destinations.
− 99 −

=== PAGE 108 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
This phenomenon is pronounced among the post-90s and post-00s generations, who are
becoming the force driving the development of cultural tourism in China. Having grown up in an era
of material abundance, the younger generation is more eager to seek spiritual fulfilment and cultural
identity through in-depth travel experiences. On the one hand, they pursue personalised experiences,
and immersive performances and folk activities happen to meet their demand for diversification. On
the other hand, they are deeply influenced by social media, cultural tourism destinations and
performance projects rapidly attract widespread attention through social media sharing, prompting a
surge of interest and participation. In addition, a higher level of education enables the younger
generations to have a deeper understanding of culture, and travel becomes an important way for them
to broaden their horizons.
This generational preference, together with the upgrading of tourists’ preferences, reshapes the
tourism market landscape, drives the cultural tourism market to continuously innovate its supply,
jointly giving rise to the rapid growth in demand for cultural tourism experiences and immersive
travel experiences. Among them, cultural tourism performances, with their unique cultural
involvement and entertainment, are attracting an increasing number of audiences.
This is demonstrated by the fact that the number of the cultural performances in China in 2023
has doubled, compared with that of in 2022, and arrived at approximately 189.3 thousand
performances in 2024. Established shows that have gained widespread recognition from both the
market and audience are anticipated to expand their number of performances to reach a broader
audience coverage. Additionally, new shows are expected to be introduced to diversify cultural
tourism performances. Therefore, the number of cultural tourism performances is forecasted to reach
approximately 324.0 thousand performances by 2029, representing a CAGR of approximately 11.3%
from 2024 to 2029.
Although China’s cultural tourism performance market experienced fluctuations due to the
negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic from 2020 to 2022, it demonstrated a strong market
rebound in 2023, which was mainly attributed to the resurgence of the domestic tourism market and
the growing demand for local cultural experience travelling. In 2024, the upward trend sustained, and
the number of audience attendance for cultural tourism performance further rebounded to
approximately 85.4 million attendance. In the following years, the tourism market is expected to
continue to recover, particularly in the popularity of short-distance domestic travel and the demands
for immersive culture experience, as well as the diversified cultural tourism performance which is
empowered by advanced technology and creative contents to significantly enhance the audience
experience. Therefore, China’s cultural tourism performance market will sustain the long-term growth
going forward. The audience attendance is projected to achieve approximately 139.9 million
attendance by 2029, representing a CAGR of approximately 10.4% from 2024 to 2029.

approximately 68.8% from 2020 to 2024. The tourism performances are normally based on the local
culture, history or traditions which are centred around specific themes, offering the audience an
immersive experience and reinforcing the distinctive characteristics of the destination. Additionally,
technological advancement has enhanced the audience engagement experience during the cultural
tourism performances. As a result, the box office receipts of cultural tourism performance are
projected to reach approximately RMB29.1 billion by 2029, representing a CAGR of approximately
12.1% from 2024 to 2029.

itself becomes an integral part of the performance, enhancing the visual spectacle. Moreover,
performances in natural settings often showcase local myths, legends, traditions and cultural practices
in an authentic manner which are deeply rooted in the region. By intertwining local history with the
natural surroundings, these performances create a profound cultural and emotional bond for travellers.
Projections indicate that the box office receipts from tourism scenery performance market is expected
to continue its upward trajectory, with a forecasted CAGR of approximately 12.3% from 2024,
reaching approximately RMB7.4 billion by 2029 and maintaining a consistent growth trend during this
period.

The diverse regional culture and extensive historical heritage of Fujian Province have
established a strong foundation for the growth of its cultural tourism market. In recent years, with the
thriving cultural tourism performance market across China, Fujian Provincial People’s Government
(福建省人民政府) is strategically developing the cultural tourism market within the province. In
2023, Fujian Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism (福建省文化和旅遊廳) reckoned the live
performance as a major driver in developing the local tourism market. The live performance market
in Fujian Province achieved a year-on-year growth rate of approximately 485.9% and 67.5% in 2023
and 2024, respectively. This initiative aims to deepen tourists’ interest for natural beauty of local
attractions into an exploration of the rich culture experience that Fujian Province offers.
On the basis that Fujian Province is enhancing its reputation as a cultural hub, the provincial
government further highlighted the concept of “cultural tourism performance +” to promote the blend
of local culture with iconic heritage spots. The wealth of cultural resources provides a rich source of
inspiration for performance creators. High-quality performance can play a critical role in driving the
growth of the cultural tourism performance market, fostering resonation with tourists. More
specifically, the province boasts stunning natural landscapes which serve as pristine backdrops for
tourism scenery performances. Leveraging the advantage of its long-standing cultural heritage and
diverse geographical landscape, tourism scenery performances in Fujian Province encompass the
potential to create substantial added value, which thus forms a driving force the cultural tourism
market in Fujian Province.
Growth Driver of China’s Cultural Tourism Performance Market
• Government regulations and policies: China’s regulations and policies have always been
conceived to be the cornerstone of creating a robust framework for growth and development. For
example, the Guiding Opinions on Promoting the Development of Cultural Tourism Performing
Arts 《( 關於促進旅遊演藝發展的指導意見》) sets the ambitious tone for the quality and branding
of cultural tourism performances, aiming to fully leverage the role of cultural tourism
− 102 −

=== PAGE 111 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
performances as an important vehicle for the integration of culture and tourism. In terms of the
policy environment, cultural tourism performance enterprises that meet the criteria for high-tech
enterprise certification can enjoy tax preferences in accordance with the law. At the same time,
the promotion of the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model in the cultural tourism performance
sector is supported. Efforts are also made to actively guide private equity funds and various
investment institutions to invest in cultural tourism performance projects. The 14th Five-Year
Plan for the Development of the Tourism Industry 《( “十四五”旅遊業發展規劃》) further
highlights the importance of integrating culture with tourism to promote cultural exchanges and
enrich the cultural connotations of tourism products. At the same time, it is proposed to build
around 30 demonstration cities to drive the continuous growth of cultural tourism consumption,
and to select more than 200 national-level clusters for night-time cultural tourism consumption.
• Robust recovery of tourism industry after pandemic: The post-pandemic resurgence of
China’s tourism sector has cultivated a favourable landscape for the expansion of cultural
tourism performance within tourist hotspots. Emerging from stifling lockdowns and travel
constraints for the paramount sanitation and health consideration, Chinese travellers became
keen on offsetting the lost travel opportunities as a result of the lockdowns and travel constraints
during the pandemic. Travellers gravitated towards domestic locations, particularly the
short-distance domestic travel and immersive culture experience travel. In 2023, domestic
tourism expenditure surged by an impressive 140.3% year-on-year, reaching approximately
RMB4.9 trillion. With the rebound in domestic travel, traveller’s attention has been diverted to
explore enriching and interactive experiences, driving a heightened demand for cultural
showcases, live entertainment and participatory events at renowned sites. Particularly, the
cultural tourism performances with the regional heritage and local traditional elements gained
popularity, offering travellers deeper connections to the locate they explore.
• Increasing demands forcultural and experiential travel:With the gradual economic recovery,
the disposable income of residents is expected to increase, which enables people to have more
capacity to pursue high-quality and personalised travel experiences. Cultural tourism
performances, particularly those rich in heritage and local culture, meet travellers’ demands
perfectly by allowing tourists to enjoy natural scenery and to experience the local history,
culture, and folk customs. These live shows transcend mere observation, enabling travellers to
find and display a seamless and strong affinity with the region’s cultural tapestry. At the same
time, the Generation Z is gradually becoming the main force in the tourism market in China. This
group enjoys a more affluent material life and places greater emphasis on experience. They opt
to explore the world and learn about different cultures through travel, and are keen on sharing
their travel experiences on social media platforms. In addition, with the rise of social media and
short video platforms, more and more travel destinations have become popular online as
“Internet-famous tourist spot”, which further stimulates people’s interest in cultural experiential
tourism.
− 103 −

=== PAGE 112 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
• Abundant regional culture cultivates vibrant cultural tourism performance:The exploration
of regional traditional cultures has emerged as a key avenue for advancing cultural development.
China boasts an immensely diverse array of regional cultural assets, showcasing its unique
traditions, historical legacies, ethnic practices and natural scenery. These intricate traditions,
deeply rooted in the histories, beliefs and principles of local populations, form a dynamic canvas
for cultural tourism performances. These traditions captivate tourists on an emotional and
intellectual level, fostering a deeper appreciation for indigenous cultures as well. Through
harnessing these resources, tourist destinations can craft genuine and immersive encounters that
can not only draw in travellers but also safeguard and showcase the distinctive cultural essence
of each locale.
Future Trends of China’s Cultural Tourism Performance Market
• Tourism scenery performance with immersive and multi-sensory experience will be
appreciated: The cultural tourism performance with natural landscape in tourism attractions
will become a defining type of touring performance. Natural landscapes often carry significant
cultural, historical and spiritual meaning for local communities and possess significant
magnetism for incoming travellers. By hosting cultural tourism performances against backdrop
of such landscapes, tourism attractions are able to showcase not just the beauty of nature but also
the stories, traditions and values inherent to the land. Additionally, cultural tourism
performances in natural settings create an immersive and multi-sensory experience for tourists,
which is far more engaging than indoor performances.
• Integration of traditional culture with modern technology: One of the most prominent trends
in China’s cultural tourism performance industry is the integration of traditional cultural
elements with modern technology. Traditional art forms and regional culture elements are being
revitalised through technological innovations. This fusion of traditional and novelty enables
cultural tourism performance to reach a broader and more digitally literate audience, especially
younger generations who are increasingly drawn to modern entertainment experiences.
• Continue to explore regional culture as performance content: Cultural tourism is increasingly
focused on authenticity. Tourists want to engage with performances that are deeply rooted in the
region’s local culture, traditions and heritage. This trend is reshaping cultural tourism
performances. Additionally, market players are encouraged to explore local cultural
characteristics and the ways to present stage content. By delving into local culture and folklore,
along with the continuous improvement from production teams, more unique and appealing
cultural tourism performances are expected to be created in the market.
• Established market players to create multiple growth curves: Market players enjoy strong
reputations are well-positioned to employ a variety of strategies to create multiple growth
curves. These market players could expand their performance repertoire or create new
performances to cater to a broader range of audience. They could also diversify their revenue
streams by developing merchandising and licensing opportunities, as well as operating tourism
properties. These strategies help such market players stay competitive, attract more audience and
maintain a long-term and sustainable business model that continuously adapts to the changing
audience tastes.

Entry Barriers of China’s Cultural Tourism Performance Market
• Barriers in geographic location and cultural profundity: Cultural tourism performances are
commercial entertainment activities that primarily showcase the regional cultural backgrounds
or local customs and traditions. The performance venues are mostly situated in tourist hotspots.
Geographical location affects both seasonality adaptability of cultural tourism performances and
performance contents, as these contents, to a great extent, rely on the specific local culture in
order to create a distinctive tourism product. Additionally, the non-replicability is also reflected
in the surrounding landscape of the performance, even more pronounced in tourism scenery
performance. The first tourism scenery performance has the first-mover advantage over the
specific landscape which is no longer available to latecomers.
• Barriers in performance content and stage arrangement: A balance between artistry,
marketability, cultural heritage and technological innovation serves as the cornerstone for
cultural tourism performance to be a blockbuster and its sustainable development afterwards. In
particular, a high degree of unity between artistic quality and marketability is the lifeblood for
cultural tourism performances. Therefore, the creators, scriptwriters and directors need to focus
on presenting modern artistic expressions and providing audience with an impressive viewing
experience. Experienced production teams can discern evolutions in tourist demands and
accurately target the position of the performance, allowing audience to resonate deeply and
empathise profoundly, thereby forming a positive word-of-mouth in the market.
• Barriers in brand effect and marketing strategy: The competitive landscape of cultural
tourism performance market in China has evolved from a small-scaled and scattered market
towards an energetic market consisting of integrated enterprises with brand value. Over years of
publicity, these enterprises will become able to build brand awareness and gain high recognition
among travellers. As a result, they have accumulated rich experience in respect of marketing
strategies, providing a solid safeguard for brands’ long-term prosperity. Cultural tourism
performances from pioneering brands are more likely to be preferred by travellers, leading to a
sustained and steady growth in audience base and forming an intractable entry barrier for new
entrants.
• Barriers in synergistic operational capability: Most established tourism performance
enterprises have shown a preference for a multi-business model. This model involves a
horizontal expansion of their businesses around the core operation of cultural tourism
performance, where the tourism entertainment products and services ancillary to the
performance content are provided to travellers to reach a diverse service portfolio. In light of the
above, enhance their competitiveness and business sustainability. This model overcomes the
limitations of a single performing program, providing a richer tourist experience and enhancing
the linkage and synergetic effects among various business segments. Under this trend,
operational capability will become increasingly important since the integration of the tourism
industry with other sectors aggravates the complexity of resource allocation, requiring the
performance team to remain agile to market dynamics in order to make timely adjustments in
response to market changes.

Traveller-to-audience Conversion Rate of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, the traveller-to-audience conversion rate
of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show was approximately 4.6%, 6.7% and 4.7%,
respectively. In 2024, the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show accounted for approximately 0.8%
of total culture tourism performance market with box office receipts of approximately RMB129.8
million and the number of audience of more than 800,000, representing a traveller-to-audience
conversion rate of approximately 4.7% among all tourists visiting Mount Wuyi in the same year. Such
rate surpassed the industry average traveller-to-audience conversion rate of approximately 1.5%.
While the conversion rate is a widely accepted metric for assessing the popularity of a show, it is also
highly sensitive in terms of fluctuations in its denominator, i.e., the total number of tourist arrivals
to a specific city. Compared with China’s top 5 most visited tourist destinations in 2024, Mount Wuyi
is generally regarded as an emerging and boutique travel destination, recording approximately 17.3
million tourist arrivals in 2024. The relatively small tourist base in Mount Wuyi City could result in
a higher traveller-to-audience conversion rate for the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show.
Therefore, relying solely on the conversion rate, a relative indicator, to assess a show’s growth
potential provides an incomplete perspective.

The Sustained Popularity of A Song of Everlasting Sorrow
As a benchmark for tourism scenery performance in China, the evolution of A Song of
Everlasting Sorrow illustrates how the popularity and commercial value of a tourism scenery
performance can be enhanced and sustained through continuous innovation and refinement. Since
2014, the production has steadily improved in both quality and scale through ongoing technical
upgrades and creative content enhancements. In 2014, the show upgraded its stage mechanics by
introducing a fully concealed stage design with computerised intelligent controls. This significantly
reduced the likelihood of mechanical failures and improved overall operational stability. In 2021, a
winter edition was launched, making it one of the few outdoor live performances in northern China
to run year-round, thus expanding the total number of annual shows. In 2024, further improvements
were made to stage effects, including enhancements to costumes, props, audio equipment, and lighting
systems, along with the addition of laser effects to elevate the visual experience.
As a result of these sustained improvements, A Song of Everlasting Sorrow achieved an
impressive CAGR of approximately 21.1% in box office revenue from 2014 to 2024. During the same
period, the number of performances increased by a factor of 3.6, while total audience attendance grew
4.7 times.

The Sustained Popularity of Impression — Lijiang
Impression — Lijiang is a large-scale tourism scenery performance which was planned, created,
and directed by the “Impression Trio”. The performance draws cultural elements from local intangible
cultural heritage skills, such as Miao silverware forging, Naxi ancient music performance, and Bai
ethnic group’s Three-Course Tea ceremony. Moreover, the leading roles are played by local ethnic
minority villagers. Among the 1,200 performers in Impression Lijiang, 90% are indigenous residents
from the foot of Yulong Snow Mountain. Due to intense competition with Lijiang Eternal Love in the
local market, the box office receipts of Impression — Lijiang declined from 2014 to 2018. However,
in 2019, the company successfully reversed this trend by strengthening the marketing and promotion
of Impression — Lijiang and bundling it with the tourism products of Yulong Snow Mountain. In

addition, to leverage the trend of travel photography, the company collaborated with local travel
photography teams at the Impression — Lijiang venue to launch a travel photography product and
packages that include performance tickets. These products focus more on cultural connotations and
unique immersive scenes, making full use of the distinctive theatre and performance resources of
Impression — Lijiang and incorporating more ethnic cultural elements, thereby further increasing the
traffic for the Impression — Lijiang performance.
Despite experiencing fluctuations in the box office receipts during the pandemic, a stable
positive trend has been observed over the past few years. Impression — Lijiang achieved a CAGR of
approximately 19.8% in box office revenue from 2020 to 2024. During the same period, the number
of performances increased by a factor of 2.1, while total audience attendance grew 2.7 times.

The Sustained Popularity of Songcheng Eternal Love
Songcheng Eternal Love is a cultural tourism performance located within the Songcheng scenic
area in Hangzhou, with a history of almost 30 years. In 2018, Songcheng Eternal Love underwent a
holographic technology upgrade. By using large-scale panoramic LED screens and holographic
projection imaging technology, combined with on-site lighting, sound, and live performances, it
vividly presented the prosperity of Songcheng and the charm of Hangzhou. In 2024, the performance
incorporated more modern elements, such as augmented reality (AR) technology. This integration of
ancient stories with modern technology created an unprecedented immersive experience.
However, unlike A Song of Everlasting Sorrow and Impression — Lijiang, Songcheng Eternal
Love is a theme park performance. Although both theme park performances and tourism scenery
performances fall within the category of cultural tourism performance, there are significant
differences between the two. Tourism scenery performances are based on specific natural landscapes
or historical sites, with the venue and performance content deeply integrated, making them difficult
to replicate. This uniqueness endows tourism scenery performances with irreplaceability, making
them a symbolic project for local tourism. In contrast, theme park performances are more flexible and
replicable. The performances are not restricted by natural conditions and can be replicated through the
construction of venues and investment in equipment.

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
The Sustained Popularity of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
The Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is the first large-scale outdoor immersive culture
tourism performance in Fujian Province and the only culture scenery performance in Mount Wuyi
which integrates the historical and culture significance of Dahongpao tea into the aesthetics of nature.
Notably, the show is selected into the Ministry of Culture and Tourism’s “2023 National Cultural
Tourism Performance Excellence Projects”.
In addition to the awards and accolades the show has obtained, we believe the sustained
popularity of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show can be illustrated in the following
dimensions:
➣ Box office receipts:The box office receipts of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
amounted to approximately RMB129.8 million in 2024, marking it the third among all the
tourism scenery performances and the ninth among all the cultural tourism performances
in terms of box office receipts in China.
According to Frost & Sullivan, box office receipt is the most direct operating-and-financial
data that reflecting the actual demand from audiences for a particular performance. High
box office receipt indicates that a large number of viewers are willing to spend money on
tickets, which not only signifies recognition of the performance content but also affirms the
efforts of the actors, directors and the entire production team. Box office receipt is also a
crucial component of the economic benefits of performing arts projects. For investors and
producers, box office performance directly influences the project’s profitability and the
confidence in its future investments.
➣ Number of performance and audience attendance: Since its debut on 29 March 2010 and
up to 31 December 2024, the show had been performed over 6,700 times and attracted more
than 9.5 million audience. The average ticket issuance rate of our show was approximately
75.7% for the year ended 31 December 2024.
➣ Traveller-to-audience conversion rate of the show: The Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show attracted more than 800,000 audience in 2024, representing a
traveller-to-audience conversion rate of approximately 4.7% among tourists visiting Mount
Wuyi City in the same year. This rate surpassed the industry average traveller-to-audience
conversion rate of approximately 1.5% in 2024. Meanwhile, the box office receipts of the
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show represented approximately 0.4% of the total
tourism spending in Mount Wuyi City in 2024.
− 114 −

=== PAGE 123 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
From a rational perspective, while the traveller-to-audience conversion rate is a commonly
used reference indicator in the tourism performance market to measure a show’s appeal
among local tourists, its applicability and comparability are influenced by various
structural factors.
• Significant Differences inTourist Resources and Scale: First-tier cities or well-known
tourist destinations may receive a significantly higher total number of tourists each
year compared to other second- and third-tier cities. Even if their tourist-to-audience
conversion rates are relatively low, the absolute number of actual audiences may far
exceed that of cities with a smaller tourist base but higher conversion rates.
• Differences in Tourist Composition: The composition of tourists in different cities
(such as the ratio of domestic to international tourists, age demographics, spending
power and length of stay) also directly affects their willingness to engage with and
spend on the performance.
• Influence of External Factors: Finally, factors such as infrastructure, frequency of
performances, marketing efforts, and pricing strategies can also impact the final
traveller-to-audience conversion rate. Cities with more frequent performances are
better positioned to capture a wider range of tourist time slots. Projects with
substantial marketing investment can enhance visibility and ticket sales, while ticket
prices directly influence the consumption threshold, thereby affecting conversion
effectiveness.
As Mount Wuyi is a destination centred on tea culture and natural heritage, drawing
a stable and high-quality influx of visitors each year, most of these tourists are
medium- to short-distance travellers with a strong willingness to engage in cultural
experiences. This audience inherently possesses a higher baseline interest and
openness to cultural products like traditional performing arts. They seek immersive
experiences connecting them to the place’s essence. In contrast, holiday crowds in
generic cities include many seeking shopping, nightlife, generic sightseeing, or
simply a getaway; cultural performing arts are often a lower priority or easily
overlooked amidst diverse options. In such case, Mount Wuyi’s characteristics and
tourist composition is more conducive to the penetration and conversion of
performing arts products. Taking into the aforementioned factors and considering that
Mount Wuyi city is able to attract approximately 12.0 million tourists on an annual
basis, which is relatively stable for domestic tourist destinations. The
traveller-to-audience conversion rate for the Impression Dahongpao Scenery Show,
being approximately 4.7% in 2024, has placed the show at a competitive level in the
tourism performance market in China, which demonstrates strong market appeal.
➣ Traveller-to-audience conversion rate in Mount Wuyi scenic area: Notably, the
traveller-to-audience conversion rate in Mount Wuyi scenic area reached approximately
18.7%. The box office receipts of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show represented
approximately 33.0% of the total tourism spending in Mount Wuyi scenic area in 2024.

While some performances that rely on large-scale marketing campaigns to boost box office
receipts and traveller-to-audience conversion rate may achieve positive results in the short term,
nonetheless, if these performances lack substantial artistic value, it is challenging to maintain lasting
vitality. In this regard, a performance team’s commitment to upgrading the performance contents for

ensured that the performance resonated with contemporary themes and artistic standards, ultimately
strengthening its long-term viability and success.
MULTI-INDUSTRY SYNERGY MODEL OF CULTURAL TOURISM PERFORMANCE
MARKET IN CHINA
China’s cultural tourism performance market has undergone a significant change, signifying
multi-industry synergy, with the introduction of novel business models such as “cultural tourism
towns + performance” and “hotels + performance”. These integrated approaches leverage the
strengths of various sectors to enhance tourist experiences and drive a linkage growth among various
business segments. The cultural tourism town model, which combines cultural tourism performance
with a cultural tourism town of a unique cultural characteristics related to the cultural tourism
performance, has also gained traction. The introduction of cultural tourism towns in the cultural
tourism industry deepens the connection between tourists and the local culture, offering a more
profound understanding of the region’s history and traditions. It also helps uncover local tourism
resources and striking a balance between developing brand intellectual property and integrating local
culture, since the extension of the industry chain enriches the tourists’ immersive experience, thereby
enhancing the appeal and recognisability of the intellectual property of cultural tourism performance
IP. Additionally, various derivatives in the cultural tourism town, such as cultural and creative
products as well as special cultural events, further realise the commercial value of the cultural tourism
performance. Going forward, these multi-industry synergy models are anticipated to keep expanding
as they do not only respond to the evolving demands of modern tourists in China’s cultural tourism
performance market but also serve as a strategic initiative to enhance cultural appreciation.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
This section summaries the main relevant PRC laws, regulations and policies, which affect the
key aspects of our cultural tourism industry.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO COMMERCIAL PERFORMANCES
In accordance with the Regulations for the Administration of Commercial Performances 《( 營業
性演出管理條例》), which was promulgated by the State Council on 7 July 2005, and subsequently
amended on 22 July 2008, 18 July 2013, 6 February 2016 and 29 November 2020, respectively;
foreign investors may legally establish performance brokerage agencies within the territory of the
PRC. To engage in commercial performance business activities, a performance brokerage agency shall
have three or more full-time performance brokers and requisite funds for the relevant business, and
shall file an application with the culture administrative department of the people’s government of a
province, autonomous region or centrally-administered municipality. The relevant culture
administrative department shall make a decision within 20 days from receipt of the application. Upon
approval, a commercial performance permit 《( 營業性演出許可證》) shall be issued. To establish a
performance venue operation entity, it shall legally complete registration with the administrative
department for industry and commerce to obtain a business license, and complete approval procedures
in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations. No entity or
individual may counterfeit, alter, rent, lend, buy or sell any commercial performance permit, approval
document or business license. Furthermore, if a performance brokerage agency engages in any
commercial performance business activity without such permit, the culture administrative department
of the people’s government at county level prohibits such behaviour and will confiscate its
performance equipment and illegal proceeds, and impose a fine in the range of eight to ten times of
its illegal proceeds. Where there are no illegal proceeds or the illegal proceeds are less than
RMB10,000, a fine ranging from RMB50,000 to RMB100,000 shall be imposed. In addition, if any
entity or individual illegally establishes a performance venue operation entity or engages in
commercial performance business activities without authorisation, the administrative department for
industry and commerce shall lawfully ban such act and impose penalties.
On 28 August 2009, the then Ministry of Culture of the PRC (currently known as the Ministry
of Culture and Tourism of the PRC (中華人民共和國文化和旅遊部)) promulgated the Implementation
Rules to theAdministrative Regulations on the Commercial Performance 《( 營業性演出管理條例實施
細則》), which was subsequently amended on 15 December 2017 and 13 May 2022, respectively. The
said rules define the commercial performance as on-site cultural and artistic performances to the
public for profit-making purposes with methods including but not limited to selling tickets or
obtaining sponsors, paying or remunerating performing entities or individuals, using the performances
as a medium for promotions or for promoting sales of products and in other profitable forms.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO HOTEL OPERATION
Regulations on Control of Security in the Hotel Industry
According to the Measures for the Control of Security in the Hotel Industry 《( 旅館業治安管理
辦法》), which was promulgated by the State Council on 10 November 1987, subsequently amended
on 8 January 2011, 29 November 2020 and 29 March 2022, respectively; and the Decision of the State
Council on Establishing Administrative License for Necessarily Retained Items Requiring
Administrative Examination and Approval 《( 國務院對確需保留的行政審批項目設定行政許可的決
− 118 −

=== PAGE 127 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
定》) promulgated by the State Council on 29 June 2004, subsequently amended on 29 January 2009
and 25August 2016, respectively, anyone who applies to operate a hotel is subject to examination and
approval by the local public security authority and must obtain a special industry license. The
Measures for the Control of Security in the Hotel Industry impose certain security control obligations
on the hotel operators. For example, the hotel must examine the identification card of any guest to
whom accommodation is provided and accurate registration of identity is required. The hotel must
also report to the local public security authority if it discovers anyone violating the law or behaving
suspiciously or an offender wanted by the public security authority. Pursuant to the Measures for the
Control of Security in the Hotel Industry, hotels which fails to obtain the special industry license may
be subject to warnings or fines up to RMB200. If a hotel initiates operation without registration, the
public security authorities shall assist the administration for industry and commerce in dealing with
the non-registration in accordance with the laws. In addition, pursuant to the Law of the PRC on
Penalties for the Violation of Public Security Administration 《( 中華人民共和國治安管理處罰法》)
which was promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (the “SCNPC”)
on 28 August 2005 and subsequently amended on 26 October 2012, and various local regulations,
hotel operators failing to obtain the special industry license may be subject to detention and fines.
Hotel operators who have obtained the special industry license but violate applicable administrative
regulations may also be subject to revocation of licenses in serious circumstances.
Regulations on Food Safety
In accordance with the Food Safety Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國食品安全法》), with was
promulgated by the SCNPC on 28 February 2009 and subsequently amended on 29 April 2021, and
the Implementation Rules of PRC the Food Safety Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國食品安全法實
施條例》), which promulgated by the State Council on 20 July 2009 and subsequently amended on 11
October 2019, the state sets up a system consisting of the supervision, monitoring and appraisal on
the food safety risks, compulsory adoption of food safety standards. To engage in food production,
sales or catering services, the business operators shall obtain a licence in accordance with the relevant
laws and regulations. Violations of these laws and measures may result in civil liabilities and
administrative penalties, such as compensation for damages, fines, suspension of manufacturing or
business operation, confiscation of tools, equipment, food ingredients and other articles used in the
illegal food production or trading, and criminal penalties in serious circumstances.
According to theAdministrative Measures for Food Operation Licensing and Record-filing 《( 食
品經營許可和備案管理辦法》), which was promulgated by the State Administration for Market
Regulation (the “SAMR”) on 15 June 2023 and became effective on 1 December 2023, entities
engaging in sales of foods and catering services within the PRC shall obtain a food operation license
which is valid for five years except for certain circumstances. Applications for a food operation
license shall be filed according to food operators’ types of operation and classification of operation
projects. Food operators shall display in prominent position their original food operation licenses or
their electronic certificate at their sites of operation. If any licensing items which are indicated on a
food operation license change, the food operator shall, within 10 business days after the changes take
place, applies to the market regulatory authority which has originally issued the license for alteration
of the operation license. Those who engage in food operation activities but fail to obtain a required
food operation license shall be punished by the local market regulatory authorities at or above the
county level according to Article 122 of the Food Safety Law of the PRC.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulations on Public Sanitation
The State Council promulgated the Administrative Regulations on Sanitation of Public Places
(《公共場所衛生管理條例》) on 1 April 1987 and subsequently amended the regulations 6 February
2016, 23 April 2019 and 6 December 2024, respectively. According to the said regulations, a hotel
must obtain a public area hygiene license before opening for business. Additionally, hotels which fail
to obtain a public area hygiene license may be subject to the following administrative penalties
depending on the seriousness of their respective activities: (i) warnings; (ii) fines; (iii) orders to
suspend business for rectification; or (iv) revocation of hygiene license. On 10 March 2011, the
National Health and Family Planning Commission (中華人民共和國國家衛生和計劃生育委員會)
promulgated the Implementation Rules of the Administrative Regulations on Sanitation of Public
Places 《( 公共場所衛生管理條例實施細則》), which came into force on 1 May 2011 and was
subsequently amended on 19 January 2016 and 26 December 2017, respectively, according to which,
hotel operators shall establish sanitation management systems and keep records of sanitation
management.
Regulation on Fire Control
Pursuant to the Fire Control Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國消防法》) which was
promulgated by the SCNPC on 29April 1998 and last amended on 29April 2021, where a construction
project that is subject to fire protection final inspection according to the law fails or is nonconforming
as established by the fire protection final inspection, it shall be prohibited from being put into use;
and any other construction project that is nonconforming as established by the random inspection
conducted under the law shall cease to be used. Article 13 of the Fire Control Law of the PRC 《( 中
華人民共和國消防法》) further provides that the constructing entity is obligated to make the safe
safety acceptance filing with the competent housing and urban-rural development authorities.
Pursuant to the Interim Provisions on theAdministration of Examination andAcceptance of Fire
Prevention Design of Construction Projects 《( 建設工程消防設計審查驗收管理暫行規定》) issued by
the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on 1 April 2020 and subsequently amended
on 21 August 2023, special construction projects that have not passed the fire prevention inspection
or have failed to pass the fire prevention inspection are prohibited from being put into use.
Construction projects other than special construction projects shall go through the fire safety
acceptance filing, and the competent housing and urban-rural development authorities shall conduct
random inspections on the fire safety acceptance of other construction projects filed. If the
construction projects fail to pass the random inspection on fire safety acceptance, such projects shall
be stopped.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO LAND
According to the Land Administration Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國土地管理法》) which
was promulgated by the SCNPC on 25 June 1986 and subsequently amended on 26 August 2019, and
the Regulations for the Implementation of the Land Administration Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共
和國土地管理法實施條例》) which was promulgated by the State Council on 27 December 1998 and
subsequently amended on 2 July 2021, the state-owned land use rights may be used by third parties

through grant, allocation, lease, capital contribution and other methods prescribed by laws. Parties

According to the Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration 《( 不動產登記暫行條例》),

According to the Civil Code of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國民法典》) promulgated by the
