From 2020 to 2024, Fujian Province experienced an increase in tourist arrivals, increasing from
approximately 372.1 million person-times approximately 649.0 million person-times with a CAGR of
approximately 14.9%, according to Frost & Sullivan. Prompted by its abundant natural scenery and
profound cultural heritage, Fujian Province aims to further tap into local cultural resources and roll
out diverse tourism productions with distinct regional features. Tourist arrivals in Fujian Province are
expected to grow continuously, reaching approximately 1,053.7 million person-times by 2029,
representing a CAGR of approximately 10.2% from 2024 to 2029. The cultural tourism market is set
to benefit from several market conditions, of which includes favourable government policies aimed
at promoting tourism. The local government has endeavoured to increase flight and railway
connections between Mount Wuyi and other major hub cities, while allocating resources towards
promoting the tourism industry. Fujian Province’s rich regional culture and extensive historical
heritage provide a solid foundation for the growth of its cultural tourism market. In recent years, as
the cultural tourism performance sector has flourished across China, the Fujian Provincial
Government has strategically focused on developing the local cultural tourism market. In 2023, the
Fujian Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism identified live performances as a key driver for
boosting local tourism. The live performance market in Fujian experienced remarkable year-on-year
growth rates of approximately 485.9% in 2023 and 67.5% in 2024. This initiative aims to deepen
tourists’ appreciation for the natural beauty of local attractions by encouraging exploration of the rich
cultural experiences that Fujian has to offer. As Fujian enhances its reputation as a cultural hub in
China, the provincial government has emphasised the concept of “cultural tourism performance+,”
promoting the integration of local culture within iconic heritage sites. The abundance of cultural
resources serves as a rich source of inspiration for performance creators. High-quality performances
can significantly drive the growth of the cultural tourism market and resonate with visitors.
Specifically, the province’s natural landscapes provide scenic backdrops for tourism performances. By
leveraging its deep-rooted cultural heritage and diverse geography, tourism performances in Fujian
have the potential to contribute high-impact value, serving as a driving force in the region’s cultural
tourism market.
Synergies between our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi,
Impression Cultural Tourism Town business and Chatang hotel business
As the home of Dahongpao tea, Mount Wuyi serves as the backdrop for our cultural tourism
service offerings. By strategically aligning our four core service offerings, we are able to generate
synergies that enhance overall tourist experiences and strengthen our competitive positioning in the
local cultural tourism market. At the heart of our business is our signature outdoor live show,
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, which captures the essence of Dahongpao tea and the natural
splendour of Mount Wuyi with natural landscape as the backdrop of the show. This performance is a
major attraction in Mount Wuyi City and is often considered as a must-see itinerary for tourists,
drawing travellers to Mount Wuyi and fuelling demand for our other tourism services. Adding to our
performance portfolio is our new Moonlight over Mount Wuyi show launched in May 2025. It serves
to diversify performance show options available in Mount Wuyi City, and offers a completely
different theatrical and cultural experience. It promotes the traditional Chinese philosophy of Zhuzi

To further enrich the tourist experience, we have been strategically developing our Impression

Continuous innovation in pursuit of excellence and a versatile professional performance team
At the core of our success lies our pursuit of excellence. Over the past decade and up to the
Latest Practicable Date, we have been introducing audience-and-performer interactive sessions and
service upgrades as well as pre-performance vibrant street shows prior to show time to engage
audiences. Notably, we have fine-tuned the performance contents for Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show during the Track Record Period. To accommodate bad weather conditions whilst
ensuring the performance can still maintain a perfect artistic presentation, we introduced a
“wind-and-rain” version of the show in March 2024. In April 2024, we engaged professional dance
instructors to provide guidance in order to elevate dance techniques and content expression.
Additionally, for the purpose of increasing the interaction between our performance team and the
audience, we introduced a “tea-offering” performance session for the show in the same month. In
respect of the “tea-making” performance of the show, we integrated original music and dance in the
session, enriching the portrayal of Dahongpao tea culture and the lives of tea artisans in May 2024.
In addition to the upgrades to the show’s performance content, we also conducted regular maintenance
to refurbish and repair our performance stage, as well as our sound and lighting systems. For example,
we undertook refurbishments of our lighting and sound systems, creating new light and shadow effects
that immerse our audience in our performances on an annual basis. This generally happened at the end
of each year. Our meticulously designed auditorium rotates 360 degrees, offering a continuously
changing viewing point. We also integrated multimedia interactive technology, allowing our audience
to engage directly with our performers, further elevating their immersive experience. These
enhancements allowed us to integrate audio-visual sensory elements into the show, solidifying its
status as one of the premier cultural events in Mount Wuyi and throughout China. The popularity of
our show is demonstrated by an average ticket issuance rate of the show amounting to approximately
75.7% for the year ended 31 December 2024 and approximately 71.4% for the six months ended 30
June 2025.
As for our Moonlight over Mount Wuyi show, given its debut not long ago, our directorial and
performance team is continuously working to improve the performance quality through constant
monitoring of feedback, regular evaluation and implementation of upgrades and tweaks.

Dual ticket sales channels translating into broader market coverage and scalability and
optimised operating performance
Our dual ticket sales channels enable us to reach a diverse range of audience. Such channels
include (i) ticket bulk sales to our ticket selling distributors who conduct onward sales of tickets and
(ii) direct sales of tickets to our audience. In particular, through ticket bulk sales to our ticket selling
distributors, we are able to gain extensive ticket-booking coverage, thereby securing the scalability
and reach of our show and amplifying our market presence across China.
We manage our ticket-booking process through formulating a standardised booking channel
management protocol and hosting promotional activities responding to seasonality, helping us strike
a balance between sales volume and yield. Said protocol also applies to management of our ticket
selling distributors, who are able to leverage their resources to capture a diverse audience base. Our
proactive ticket-selling management provides resilience against variable market conditions, helping
us minimise seating vacancy rate. Furthermore, engaging ticket selling distributors allows us to stay
abreast of evolving market trends, allowing timely responses to environmental changes. The
engagement of ticket selling distributors was high-yielding, recording a segment revenue contribution
of approximately RMB53.2 million, RMB126.2 million, RMB120.0 million, RMB44.2 million and
RMB46.6 million for the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended
30 June 2024 and 2025, respectively.
Our dual ticket sales channels ensure broader ticket sales coverage, and therefore enable us to
focus on solidifying and upgrading our signature show and creating our new show, while further
exploring other synergistic opportunities surrounding our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business
and improving our Chatang hotel business. Such an operating model allows us to concentrate our
efforts on fortifying our core business while exploring new business opportunities in the broader
cultural tourism market.

Continue focusing on innovation and reinforce the leadership position of our Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show
We plan to enhance the viewing experience and artistic value of our signature show through an
upgrade initiative designed to meet growing audience demands. Key improvements will focus on
innovating our show’s contents and presentation, as well as upgrading hardware and venue facilities.
This includes a complete overhaul of the show’s structure; an upgrade of the performance script; the
addition of new segments featuring rituals with red silk, tea picking, and tea production in terraced
fields; along with re-recording existing dialogue. Such plans align with our pursuit of excellence in
respect of the quality and appeal of our show. During the Track Record Period, we have fine-tuned
the performance contents of our signature show four times. For details, see “— Our Competitive
Strengths — Continuous innovation in pursuit of excellence and a versatile professional performance
team” in this section. The sound system will undergo complete renovation, and the lighting system
will be revamped to enhance the audience experience. We believe these enhancements will enrich the
performance content, increase interactiveness, and deeply engage our audience, further establishing

our show as a premium platform for exploring the culture of Dahongpao tea in Mount Wuyi. By

experience and enhance customer satisfaction.

Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
Overview
Our signature Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is the cornerstone of our business and is
a standout production in the acclaimed Impression series of large-scale outdoor performances. It is
also the first large-scale outdoor scenic performance in Fujian Province according to Frost & Sullivan.
The show is a testament to the artistry of three famous filmmakers and directors being Mr. Zhang
Yimou (張藝謀), Ms. Wang Chaoge (王潮歌) and Mr. Fan Yue (樊躍), collectively known as the
Impression Power Trio (印象鐵三角). This talented team is well known for its capabilities in
innovative storytelling and creating immersive experiences for audience, which has successfully made
its Impression series popular across various scenic locations in China and has uniquely positioned
them in the field of creating large-scale performances in the cultural tourism market. According to
Frost & Sullivan, our signature show ranked third in terms of box office receipts among tourism
scenery performances, and tenth in terms of box office receipts among all cultural tourism
performances in China in 2024.
We conduct our show in Mount Wuyi, a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage Site and
part of the organisation’s Network of Biosphere Reserves. Our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery
Show serves as a prime example of the integration of nature and culture. The performance is
surrounded by beautiful outdoor scenes of mountains, flowing river and ancient architecture, featuring
tea culture as its core theme. We aim to leave audiences feeling that their trips to Mount Wuyi have
been worthwhile, allowing them to experience a performance enriched by integrated natural and
cultural characteristics. Our show’s narrative brings together elements of local culture and history,
inviting the audience to explore the connections between nature and humanity. Each performance is
not merely a display of artistic talent; instead, it is an immersive journey that resonates with the soul
of the region. Our audience experiences the heritage and natural scenery of Mount Wuyi, where the
beauty of the landscape enhances the storytelling, creating a multi-sensory experience that is
engaging, and entertaining. We take pride in the saying: “If you miss Impression — Dahongpao, you
miss the highlight of Mount Wuyi”. As we continuously fine-tune our Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show, it innovates while preserving the traditional Chinese culture elements, which serves to
enhance the vitality of Chinese culture and deepen the integration of cultural and tourism
characteristics of Mount Wuyi, allowing the concept of “Performing Arts + Tourism” to shine.
Since its debut on 29 March 2010, our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show has achieved
remarkable success. The average ticket issuance rate of our show was approximately 69.4%, reflecting
a strong audience demand and enthusiasm for our performances for the six months ended 30 June
2025. As at the Latest Practicable Date, we had performed Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
over 6,700 times and attracted more than 9.4 million in audiences since its debut in 2010. For a
detailed illustration of the popularity of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, see “Industry
Overview — Competitive Landscape of China’s Cultural Tourism Performance Market — The
Sustained Popularity of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show” in this prospectus.

BUSINESS
This is our top-grossing and signature business segment historically and during theTrack Record
Period. For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended 30 June
2024 and 2025, revenue from our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show was approximately
RMB57.6 million, RMB135.7 million, RMB129.8 million, RMB47.9 million and RMB49.1 million,

respectively.
Performance
Our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show takes place at night and each performance lasts for
approximately one hour. Our show begins with an enchanting introduction that sets the tone for the
evening, inviting audience to embark on a journey through the beauty and heritage of Mount Wuyi.
As the performance unfolds, our audience are treated to a series of vignettes that explore the
significance of Mount Wuyi Dahongpao tea culture, the local environment and the human experience.
Our 360-degree rotating auditorium allows for continuous movement and transformation of
different visuals on the performance stage, keeping the audience engaged and captivated. Performers
navigate the rotating auditorium, utilising artistic expressions to convey the emotions embedded in the
narrative. The integration of multimedia elements enhances the storytelling, providing visual context
that enriches the audience’s understanding of the cultural themes presented and appreciation of
aesthetics.
Seven chapters of Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
Ashow woven around the theme of Dahongpao tea, the performance portrays a tale, divided into
seven chapters that unveil the essence of MountWuyi and its Dahongpao tea culture. The performance
immerses our audience in the seven chapters of our show through the monologue of a tea house owner.
The following table illustrates the main theme of each of the seven chapters of our Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show.

Girl calm their minds and experience the beauty of nature.

Preparatory Stage
Obtaining the Exclusive Performance Right
Back in 2008, Fujian Mount Wuyi Cultural Tourism Group, one of our Controlling Shareholders,
sought to create a large-scale scenery performance project that could showcase local characteristics
of MountWuyi for the purposes of enhancing MountWuyi’s tourism appeal. To this end, Fujian Mount
Wuyi Cultural Tourism Group, as the project initiator and the promoter of our Company, decided to
(i) collaborate with Impression Art Development to jointly produce the Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show; and (ii) as one of the promoters, initiated the establishment of our Company as the
operating entity to curate the show with an exclusive performance right. To achieve this, each of
Fujian Mount Wuyi Cultural Tourism Group, Impression Art Development, and our Company agreed
upon a tripartite arrangement to outline the rights and responsibilities in respect of the show. Pursuant
to the tripartite arrangement, Fujian Mount Wuyi Cultural Tourism Group was responsible for the
overall coordination to advance the project, Impression Art Development was responsible for the
initial design and direction of the show; and we were tasked with implementing of this performance
project and curating the show exclusively. Spearheaded by Impression Power Trio, Impression Art
Development is a cultural and tourism performance creative production and copyright operation
company established in 2006. ImpressionArt Development is an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of
Sanxiang Impression and is principally engaged in creating, exhibiting and selling artworks, as well
as providing art consulting services. Sanxiang Impression is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange
(000863.SZ) and is primarily engaged in cultural business and real estate business. The cultural
business sector of Sanxiang Impression has been conducted through its wholly-owned subsidiary,
Impression Art Development. As at the Latest Practicable Date, Impression Art Development had
launched more than 20 cultural tourism shows. In 2003, Impression Art Development pioneered live
performances in China, with the production of Impression series, with Impression — Liu Sanjie
(印象劉三姐) being the first live show performance in the same year. As at the Latest Practicable
Date, the Impression series consisted of eight performances, Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
being one of them.
The exclusivity will continue according to an exclusive intellectual property rights authorisation
framework agreement between Impression Art Development and our Company, which will constitute
a non-exempt continuing connected transaction upon Listing. See “Continuing Connected Transaction
— Summary of our Continuing Connected Transactions” in this prospectus for details. Our exclusive
entitlement to curate and perform the show provides us with a distinct competitive edge as the
undisputed market leader in the tourism scenery performance market and cultural tourism
performance market in China.

BUSINESS
According to Frost & Sullivan, a successful performance relies not only on creativity and design
but also on a professional project management team to ensure it achieves the desired socio-economic
effects. In the initial preparatory stage of each performance, the directorial team and the performance
team need to collaborate closely to define the overall framework and development direction of the
performance. Specifically, the directorial team is primarily responsible for proposing creative and
technical solutions and making adjustments to the performance content, lineup and technical effects,
such as sound and lighting suggestions to ensure an engaging viewing experience. The performance
team is responsible for performing the show and providing audience feedback to the directorial team,
such that the responsible staff can provide more effective improvement suggestions. As the project
progresses, the performance team gradually takes on more daily management and decision-making
responsibilities, offering practical improvement suggestions for the performance’s content and format
based on market responses, and coordinating resources to support these adjustments. Once the
performance enters a stable operational phase, the main creative and execution responsibilities,
representing the duties to refine and improve the show content, will gradually shift to the performance
team, which will not only need to maintain the quality of the performance but also expand its
influence and continue to innovate. During the operational phase, the role of the directorial team
becomes relatively limited, as it is the performance team that better understands the real-time
audience feedback and can therefore provide more effective and practical improvement suggestions
attributable to its day-to-day performance. In light of the above, our Directors are of the view that (i)
our reliance upon Impression Art Development is limited; and (ii) the current success of the
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is inseparable from our performance of the show since 2010.

Operation Stage
Training, Rehearsal and Preparation
Preparing for the performance of our show involves rigorous training and rehearsals that bring
together the diverse talents of our performance team. The performance team primarily consists of
professionally trained actors who are the graduates of Mount Wuyi Tourism Vocational School (武夷
山旅遊職業中專學校), Zhang Yimou Lijiang Art School (張藝謀灕江藝術學校), and other provincial
− 171 −

=== PAGE 180 ===
BUSINESS
art schools. Our performance team also consists of descendants of tea-farming families, each
contributing their unique tea-farming skills and backgrounds to the production. This blend infuses the
show with authentic cultural insights and a deep affective connection to the local culture that has
shaped their lives.
A comprehensive training and rehearsal program is conducted over a period of six months,
allowing our performance team to refine their performances and ensure seamless integration of the
various elements required for the show. This includes choreographed movements, music and
interactions with the stage design. The performers undergo extensive training not only in their artistic
disciplines but also in the cultural narratives they are portraying, ensuring that every aspect of the
show is authentic and engaging.
Technical rehearsals are also conducted, focusing on the synchronisation of lighting and sound
effects, and multimedia elements with the live performances. This intricate coordination is crucial to
creating the immersive experience that audience have come to expect. Every detail is meticulously
planned, from the timing of lighting and sound cues to the positioning of performers on stage, and the
manipulation of our 360-degree rotating auditorium, ensuring a polished and professional
presentation.
Our performance team is led by our art troupe director, Ms. Wu Meiqiu (吳美球). She has
participated in the planning and execution of several performance projects, demonstrating exceptional
organisational skills and leadership capabilities. Ms. Wu is an accredited Exemplary Virtuous and
Versatile Artist in Nanping City (南平市德藝雙馨文藝家). As the director of our art troupe, Ms. Wu
is responsible for the daily management of the performance of our signature show. She is capable of
maximising the strengths of each of our performers, promoting the integration of artistic creation with
audience demands, ensuring each performance offers a unique experience to our audience. Ms. Wu’s
leadership style emphasises openness and innovation, encouraging our performance team to explore
new artistic presentations.

There are a number of individuals and entities which are involved in our ticket sales network.
These individuals and entities include ticket selling distributors and sales facilitators, which are our
non-contracting parties in terms of ticket sales.
• Ticket selling distributors: Our ticket selling distributors consist of travel agencies and
ticket agencies. They are our direct contracting parties in terms of ticket sales. They
purchase our show tickets and conduct onward sales of tickets to audience. They conduct
payments to us directly and hence are our customers on our financial statements.
• Sales facilitators: Sales facilitators are local individuals and tourism-related business
entities such as hotels, restaurants and taxi drivers as well as online ticket sales platforms
such as Klook and Ctrip, who may approach our ticket selling distributors to procure tickets
for sale. To the best knowledge of our Company, they approach our ticket selling
distributors for tickets demanded directly from travellers to Mount Wuyi who want to
watch our show. Sales facilitators are not our contracting parties. They exist in our ticket
sales network merely because some travellers may approach them to purchase show tickets.

Sales to ticket selling distributors
Selection and engagement of ticket selling distributors
We enter into standardised ticket bulk sales master agreements with our ticket selling
distributors on an annual basis. Our ticket selling distributors have to log into our ticket management
system with their specific login usernames and passwords to place purchase orders.
We have generally adopted the public bidding process for the selection of ticket selling
distributors to ensure that they possess requisite credentials and qualifications, despite it not being
mandatory under the relevant PRC laws and regulations for us to go through such a public bidding
process. In some exceptional circumstances, we may follow a selection protocol, pursuant to which
we conduct screenings and reference checks to assess the credibility and experience for those ticket
selling distributors which were not selected through the public bidding process. Such screenings and
reference checks ensured that these ticket selling distributors are reliable and experienced to conduct
onward ticket sales. Additionally, we have put market investigation measures in force to monitor the
sales activities of our ticket selling distributors. These measures are primarily implemented for the
purposes of deterring and detecting price irregularity. See the subsection below headed “— Ticket
Sales Management” for the details of our market investigation measures to monitor the sales activities
of our ticket selling distributors.
Key terms of bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements
A bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreement has to be entered into between our Company and
the ticket selling distributor either following the public bidding process or our selection protocol. The
key terms of our bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements are set out below:
Term One year

volume, varies from each ticket selling distributor. It is based on each

round of bidding process prior to an engagement. During the Track
Record Period, the average annual sales volume target ranged from
4,950 to 9,000. If a ticket selling distributor fails to meet the sales

Company will not be refunded.

Settlement method Each ticket selling distributor will be issued a user account with a
specific login username and password under our ticket management
system, through which the ticket selling distributor shall place the
purchase orders and make prepayments to us prior to our issuance of
tickets. Prepayments are typically made via bank transfer, or taken by
POS portable machine. Prepayments will thereafter be recorded on the
ticket management system.
Credit term Our ticket selling distributors purchase our show tickets through their
prepayments to our Company, deduction of which will occur upon our
issuance of show tickets to them.
Performance deposit As a prerequisite for a ticket selling distributor to be formally engaged
by us, it is obliged to pay a fixed amount (with a minimum of
RMB10,000) as performance deposit, which serves as a minimum
guarantee of income for us. Such fixed amount varies for each ticket
selling distributor, which is determined with reference to the sales
volume target in the relevant ticket bulk sales master agreement. The
performance deposit must be paid within three business days from the
date of the ticket bulk sales master agreement.
The performance deposit may be refunded or used as prepayment for
tickets sold, depending on how much of the sales volume target is
achieved, as specified in the agreement. However, if the ticket selling
distributor fails to achieve 50% of its sales volume target, none of the
performance deposit may be refunded.
Credit assessment Each ticket selling distributor is allocated a credit assessment score as
score a means for us to keep track of the distributor’s compliance with our
ticket selling requirements. The annual credit assessment form is
annexed to our ticket bulk sales master agreements, with scores
determined based on the price of tickets sold. If we become aware that
the ticket selling distributor violated our prescribed policy for sale of
tickets (including onwards sale of our tickets at a price lower than the
prescribed price), a penalty will be imposed (by way of confiscation of
a certain amount of the quality deposit according to specific
circumstances specified in the agreement) and the credit assessment
score may be deducted.
If the ticket selling distributor’s annual credit assessment score falls
below 80 out of 100, we may terminate the bilateral ticket bulk sales
master agreement, and the distributor will be disqualified from being
our ticket selling distributor in the following year.
− 176 −

=== PAGE 185 ===
BUSINESS
Quality deposit Quality deposit serves as an incentive for the ticket selling distributors
to achieve higher sales volume, and also as a deterrent in respect of
violation by ticket selling distributors of our prescribed policy for sale
of tickets. Upon the sale of each ticket, the ticket selling distributor
shall pay an extra fee per ticket sold as quality deposit. The amount of
quality deposit payable per ticket varies according to the type of ticket
sold, and shall be settled at the same time along with the prepayment for
each ticket sold, prior to the issuance of tickets. The amount of quality
deposit that is refundable is calculated based on the credit assessment
score and the actual number of tickets sold by the ticket selling
distributor during the term of the agreement (whereby a higher sales
volume will result in a higher refundable amount). However, if the ticket
selling distributor fails to achieve 75% of its sales volume target, none
of the quality deposit may be refunded.Also, as mentioned above, if we
become aware that the ticket selling distributor violated our prescribed
policy for sale of tickets, a certain amount of the quality deposit may be
confiscated by us. Any refundable amount of quality deposit shall be
settled after we complete the audit of the number of tickets sold by each
of the ticket selling distributors at the end of the term (generally at the
end of the financial year).
Early termination We have the right to terminate the bilateral ticket bulk sales master
right agreements when:
i) the ticket selling distributor’s annual credit assessment score is
lower than 80 out of 100 as mentioned above;
ii) the ticket selling distributor fail to pay the performance deposit to
us within the time frame as stipulated in the relevant ticket bulk
sales master agreements; and
iii) the ticket selling distributor breached the terms of the agreement
when conduct ticket sales and was penalised by relevant
authorities. In such case, no performance deposit or quality deposit
shall be refundable.
Refund of tickets Unless due to force majeure, such as adverse weather or the special
seating arrangements, we are not obligated to refund once show tickets
are issued, which is in line with the market practice as confirmed by
Frost & Sullivan.
Renewal Bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements are renewed on an annual
basis.

Sales facilitators
Our ticket selling distributors consist of travel agencies and ticket agencies. To the best
knowledge of our Company, the ticket selling distributors, in their ordinary course of ticket sales, may
also be approached by local individuals and tourism-related business entities such as hotels,
restaurants and taxi drivers, as well as online ticket sales platforms such as Klook and Ctrip (the
“Sales Facilitators”) for tickets demanded directly from the travellers to Mount Wuyi who want to
watch our show. The Sales Facilitators were not our contracting parties and the terms of our ticket
bulk sales master agreements do not apply to them; therefore, we do not maintain a record of Sales
Facilitators.
According to Frost & Sullivan, it is not uncommon for tourists to approach the Sales Facilitators
to purchase show tickets. Our PRC Legal Advisers have also confirmed that sales of tickets to Sales
Facilitators is a normal market conduct and is not in contravention of any relevant PRC laws and
regulations.
As our non-contracting parties, Sales Facilitators are not under our direct management.
However, since all of our audience can provide feedback and complaints on the official Fujian
Consumer Platform, we may become aware of any price irregularity caused by the Sales Facilitators
and take necessary actions accordingly. Based on the above, our Directors are of the view that the
existence of Sales Facilitators does not disrupt our ticket sales network.
Previous sales arrangement involving authorised agents
Prior to 15 January 2025, our ticket sales model involved authorised agents as well. Authorised
agents are mainly individuals including tour guides, tea business operators and owners of small-sized
local companies. Our ticket selling distributors were given the autonomy to nominate their authorised
agents to assist their ticket sales, and these authorised agents conducted payments on behalf of ticket
selling distributors to us. In such cases, each of the relevant ticket selling distributor and the
authorised agent must execute a tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreement with our Company. In
light of the above, authorised agents are our direct contracting parties in terms of ticket sales.
Nonetheless, they are not our direct customers on our financial statements as their payments are made
on behalf of the relevant ticket selling distributors and the sales volume by an authorised agent will
be counted towards the actual sales volume of the relevant ticket selling distributor.
To the best knowledge of our Company, these authorised agents may also be approached by Sales
Facilitators for the procurement of tickets on an ad-hoc basis. However, we do not directly deal with
these Sales Facilitators as they are not our contracting parties. For details of Sales Facilitators, see
“— Sales Facilitators” above in this section.

Once a ticket selling distributor decided to engage an authorised agent to meet the requisite sales
volume targets, and that authorised agent was responsible for making payment to us for placing orders
for the show tickets on behalf of the corresponding ticket selling distributor, we required that a
tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreement be entered into between the relevant ticket selling
distributor, the authorised agent, and our Company. Such tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreements
shall be signed prior to any payment to us by the authorised agent. Specifically, a ticket selling
distributor firstly executes the bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreement with our Company,
following which a tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreement will be executed if the ticket selling
distributor engages an authorised agent to meet the requisite sales volume targets, and that authorised
agent will be responsible for making payment to us for placing orders for the show tickets, on behalf
of the corresponding ticket selling distributor. This typically happens shortly after the engagement of
ticket selling distributors, upon the completion of the public bidding process or our selection protocol.
There is no difference in respect of key terms between bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements
and tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreements. See the subsection headed “— Key terms of
bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements” above for details.

Once a tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreement is executed, each of the ticket selling
distributor and the authorised agent thereof has become our contracting parties. Our sales department
is responsible for keeping all ticket bulk sales master agreements, so that we can check the lists of
our ticket selling distributors and their authorised agents. Currently, we have a ticket selling
distributor management system to record all of our ticket selling distributors for book keeping
purpose. Additionally, pursuant to the ticket bulk sales master agreements, it is further stipulated that
(i) the sales volume generated by the authorised agent will count towards the sales volume of the
relevant ticket selling distributor; and (ii) payments for ticket sales by an authorised agent must be
made directly through our online ticket selling system or to the corresponding ticket selling
distributor.
To the best knowledge of our Directors, most of our ticket selling distributors prefer to engage
authorised agents, as it could broaden ticket sales coverage and help them meet their sales volume
targets as stipulated in the ticket bulk sales master agreements. Our Directors are also of the view that
the authorised agents were engaged in a broad range of industries and have different connections that
facilitated sales of tickets. According to Frost & Sullivan, it is a market practice for ticket selling
distributors and their business partners to collaborate together as social units for sales of tickets,
given Mount Wuyi City is a relatively small city. As advised by our PRC LegalAdvisers, the tripartite
ticket bulk sales master agreements entered into by our ticket selling distributors and their authorised
agents with respect to their onwards sales of tickets are legally binding on the parties thereto.
In respect of the payments from authorised agents to our Company, each of the authorised agents
has confirmed that the payments directly made to our Company were valid and without recourse. The
Joint Sponsors have also conducted due diligence including (i) conducting interviews with each of the
authorised agents in connection with their payments to our Company; and (ii) reviewing the relevant
tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreements. Based on the due diligence, the Joint Sponsors (i) have
noted that once show tickets were issued, no refund of payments were allowed in normal
circumstances; (ii) did not note any dispute with respect to the payments made by the authorised
agents; and (iii) did not indicate otherwise that payments from the authorised agents appeared to be
invalid or were underlined by recourse from other parties.

Ticket sales management
We believe that effective management of our ticket selling distributors is crucial to the success
of our ticket sales. In addition to the responsibilities as stipulated in the bilateral ticket bulk sales
master agreements, we have adopted a ticket selling distributor management policy. According to this
policy, we have the right to, among others, (i) require ticket selling distributors to adopt our ticket
sales policy in the manner as we specify and (ii) impose penalties on, or terminate business
relationship with ticket selling distributors should we detect any irregularities in their onward ticket
sales activities, or any audience lodges a serious complaint supported by proof of irregularities of a
ticket selling distributor.
In cases where authorised agents were nominated by our ticket selling distributors, as the
authorised agents were our direct contracting parties, we were able to manage and have control over,
the authorised agent in terms of the performance of contractual obligations. According to Frost &
Sullivan, it is not uncommon for market players in the tourism scenery performance market and
cultural tourism performance market to rely on ticket selling distributors and their authorised agents
for ticket sales. Our ticket selling distributors are responsible for managing their own authorised
agents by placing the same onward sales standards we specify in the bilateral ticket bulk sales master
agreements.

We would not directly manage and monitor the sales activities of authorised agents since they
are directly nominated by the ticket selling distributors. If we become aware of any misconduct of an

the required price range as stipulated in the tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreement. Any price

reputation. See “Risk Factors —We may encounter reputation damage if there is any price irregularity

complaint from the audience.
As part of our enhanced internal control measures to reduce the cumbersome and

multiple ticket selling distributors, we ceased entering into tripartite ticket bulk sales master

made through pre-registered corporate bank accounts of the relevant ticket selling distributors,

Information of pre-registered corporate bank accounts is provided by the relevant ticket selling

Pricing
As confirmed by our PRC Legal Advisers, there is no relevant PRC law or regulation governing
the ticket prices of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show. Therefore, the pricing of the show
tickets to provision our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is market-based. Nonetheless, we are
required to adopt clearly marked price (明碼標價) pursuant to the rules set by the local pricing
authority. The implementation of market-based pricing and the requirement to clearly mark ticket
prices in accordance with the relevant provisions of the competent pricing authorities facilitates
market order and prevention of price fraud, thereby maintaining market stability and protecting the
legitimate rights and interests of consumers and operators, pursuant to the Pricing Law of the People’s
Republic of China 《( 中華人民共和國價格法》) ( the “PRC Pricing Law”). The clear marking of
prices enables the competent pricing authorities to effectively prevent fraudulent practices and protect
consumers’ rights and interests. The competent pricing authority is also entitled to conduct random
inspections in accordance with the PRC Pricing Law. We have two types of ticket prices: direct sales
price applicable to our audience, and settlement price in respect of ticket bulk sales applicable to our
ticket selling distributors (which is pre-agreed in the bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements).

The settlement price offered to our ticket selling distributors was relatively lower than the direct
sales prices offered to our audience, primarily due to the advantage of bulk sales in a win-win scenario
where our ticket selling distributors can be incentivised to conduct onward ticket sales in a motivated
manner, and at the same time, we can benefit from wider audience reach by virtue of the broader
market coverage. Therefore, we are of the view that offering ticket selling distributors certain price
discounts allows for rapid sales of tickets and achieves a higher ticket issuance rate of our Impression
— Dahongpao Scenery Show. Adjustments for resale prices are reasonably made, taking into account
audience demand during peak and off-peak seasons. Additionally, the ticket prices adopted by ticket
selling distributors and authorised agents are governed by terms stipulated in the relevant ticket sales
master agreements.

BUSINESS
During the Track Record Period and to the best knowledge of our Directors, no tickets were sold
by our ticket selling distributors or their authorised agents at a price below the minimum retail price
as stipulated in the relevant ticket sales master agreements. Typically, we monitor the ticket price
through market investigation by our sales personnel. Our sales personnel also conduct sample checks
on various online platforms to monitor the actual selling price of tickets sold by the ticket selling
distributors. We also adopt a quota system which limits the total number of tickets that can be
requested by the ticket selling distributors under the ticket bulk sales master agreements. The number
of tickets that can be requested ranges from 20 to 40 on a daily basis. Once the quota is reached, the
ticket selling distributors may opt to purchase show tickets from other ticket selling distributors.
Nonetheless, in a situation where there are seats available for the show, the ticket selling distributors
may purchase additional show tickets after 12:00 pm of that day. Each of our show tickets is issued
for a specific performance on the indicated date. If any audience holding a show ticket cannot attend
due to personal reasons, we do not allow refunds in normal circumstances unless due to force majeure
events such as bad weather conditions. In light of the above, our Directors are of the view that we have
adopted effective measures to reduce the risk of cannibalisation. Direct sales price in respect of direct
sales of tickets to our audience is available at our ticket selling points. In determining the ticket price,
we take into account the local economic conditions and the disposable income of the target audience.
This ensures that tickets remain accessible to a broad range of travellers while maximising our
revenue.
Payment
We generally require full payment before we issue show tickets to our audience in respect of
direct sales of tickets to our audience, as well as to our ticket selling distributors who conduct onward
sales of tickets. During the Track Record Period, payments from our ticket selling distributors were
primarily conducted through bank transfer, and in other cases, through point of sale system (POS).
Many of our ticket selling distributors are locally based in Mount Wuyi. They opt to come directly
to our ticket selling points for the settlement of payment. Therefore, our finance department also
adopts POS to take payment. Payments from the ticket selling distributors through POS will be
automatically recorded on our bank account.
For the year ended 31 December 2024, some of the payments received from our ticket selling
distributors under bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements were settled through third-party
payors. See the subsection headed “Third-party payments” for details.
Once our show tickets are issued, we generally do not allow ticket refunds, save for force
majeure events such as bad weather conditions. Historically and during the Track Record Period, we
did not experience any material ticket refund requests, either from our ticket selling distributors or
audience. For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023, 2024, and the six months ended 30 June 2025,
the total number of tickets that were refunded to our ticket selling distributors and audience was
1,407, nil, 3,877, and 735, accounting for approximately 0.4%, nil%, 0.5%, and 0.2% of the total
number of tickets sold during the respective period.

Background of events in 2022 and 2023
For the two years ended 31 December 2022 and 2023, we engaged 49 and 50 ticket selling
distributors, respectively. Many of these ticket selling distributors nominated their own respective
authorised agent(s) to conduct onward sales of ticket to assist them to achieve the sales volume target
before the end of the year. Tripartite bulk sales master agreements were entered into among our
Company, ticket selling distributors and authorised agents. According to the terms of our tripartite
ticket bulk sales master agreement, the sales volume generated by the authorised agent would count
towards the sales volume of the relevant ticket selling distributor.
• Bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements: For the two years ended 31 December 2022
and 2023, there were six and three ticket selling distributors, respectively, which decided
not to nominate authorised agents and therefore, these distributors only entered into
bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements with our Company. These ticket selling
distributors conducted payments to us directly for ticket sales. Nonetheless, to the best

Third-party payments which occurred in 2024
In light of the aforesaid cumbersome and time-consuming verification procedure due to the
concurrent nomination of authorised agents by multiple ticket selling distributors, we have decided
to cease adopting tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreements, whilst predominantly pursuing
bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements since 2024 (“New Arrangement”). Under this New
Arrangement, we would only need to deal with one contracting party only. This could eliminate
situations of payments not having been explicitly identified for a specific ticket selling distributor.
Nonetheless, as some of our ticket selling distributors had their own long-acquainted business
partners who were authorised agents, we still executed eight tripartite ticket bulk sales master
agreements in 2024 upon the adoption of the New Arrangement, considering that (i) these authorised
agents may be easily identified given their long-established relationship with our ticket selling
distributors; and (ii) even if an incoming payment is unidentified with the name of the associated
ticket selling distributor, there would not be undue hardship for us to identify the payor for book
keeping and sales volume target verification purposes as we are well aware of their relationships.
For the year ended 31 December 2024, we dealt with 50 ticket selling distributors with which
we entered into bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements, amongst which there were eight ticket
selling distributors who notified us of their intentions to nominate their own authorised agents. Upon
consideration as mentioned above, we decided to exempt these eight ticket selling distributors from
the New Arrangement. Accordingly, we executed eight tripartite ticket bulk sales master agreements,
and 42 bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements in 2024, respectively.
• Bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements: Following the adoption of the New
Arrangement in 2024, many of the then authorised agents who were contractual parties
became non-contracting parties. Despite the adoption of the NewArrangement, some of the
non-contracting parties who were the then individual authorised agents were still
accustomed to settle payments to us directly. In the view of our Directors, these
non-contracting parties who were the then authorised agents may not be readily and
immediately accustomed to the change, resulting in the continuity of their direct payment
to us. For example, there was also one former authorised agent who still made direct
payment to us without a ticket bulk sales master agreement in 2024. We believe it was the
behavioural inertia of those former authorised agents that gave rise to such payment, which
constituted third-party payments in 2024. Additionally, under the bilateral ticket bulk sales
master agreements, we erred in comprehending that a non-contracting party, such as the
spouse and/or legal representative, could represent the relevant ticket selling distributor
during the performance of a bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements. It was not until

Views of industry expert
According to Frost & Sullivan, it is not uncommon in China’s cultural tourism performance
market for entities to settle payments through third-party payors, primarily because (i) using a sole
proprietor or local small-sized company’s operator or his/her spouse, legal representative’s personal
bank account provides greater cash flow and settlement flexibility, which is particularly beneficial for
small and mid-sized ticket selling distributors with limited financial resources, especially when
payments of quality deposits and performance bonds are required prior to ticket issuance; and (ii)
opening a corporate bank account could be cumbersome.

View of our PRC Legal Advisors
Based on the review of internal control procedure and all mandatory requirements for
transactions adopted by our Group, our PRC Legal Advisors have advised that, for the year ended 31
December 2024, (i) there was no claim lodged by any third-party payors; nor had we been asked to
make repayments; (ii) the third-party payments were backed by legitimate underlying transactions,
i.e., sales of tickets are commercial activities; (iii) there was no concealment or misrepresentation of
the origin or nature of any criminal proceeds or income derived from such proceeds, indicating the
risk of concluding that these payments constituted money laundering is low, nor did they involve any
situation that would lead to contravention of mandatory requirements under the prevalent PRC laws
and regulations; (iv) we had not been subject to any inquiry, investigation or administrative penalties
by the competent government authorities concerning the PRC tax laws and regulation as a result of
the third-party payments we received; and (v) once a third-party payment arrangement has been made,
it comes into legal effect and cause binding obligations on each of the parties under the third-party
payment arrangement pursuant to the PRC Civil Code.
Based on the foregoing, our PRC Legal Advisors are of the view that the third-party payments
for the year ended 31 December 2024 were not in contravention of the prevalent PRC laws and
regulations.
Cessation of third-party payments
As part of the enhanced internal control measures, we ceased entering into tripartite ticket bulk
sales master agreements and no longer directly deal with authorised agents. Since 15 January 2025,
upon the execution of all bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreements, all third-party payments have
ceased and we enhanced our internal control measures to prevent the occurrence of third-party
payments going forward. For details of the enhanced internal control measures, see below subsection
headed “Enhanced internal control measure”. Based on their historical settlement records and the
absence of litigations in respect of third-party payers, their respective shareholders and directors, we
believe that the cessation of the third-party payments did not have, nor will have any material impact
on our business operations and financial results, given that (i) the historical sales of tickets were
genuine transactions; and (ii) the popularity of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show will
continue to incentivise the ticket selling distributors to conduct onward sales of tickets as there is a
genuine ticket demand from audience. Such belief is based on the following considerations:
(i) during the Track Record Period, all the third-party payments were related to genuine ticket
sales of our Company and genuine ticket requests from our ticket selling distributors and
their authorised agents;
(ii) we have not encountered any incident demanding us to return payment in relation to
relevant ticket sales;
(iii) nothing came to our attention that would cause our Directors to doubt the genuineness of
relevant transactions or the good faith of relevant parties involved;
− 192 −

=== PAGE 201 ===
BUSINESS
(iv) to the best knowledge of our Directors and after making reasonable enquiries, we
understand that our ticket selling distributors have become able and willing to cooperate
with the payment arrangement for the purpose of preventing third-party payment;
(v) since 15 January 2025, there has been no third-party payment issue following the
implementation of our enhanced internal control measure (see below for the details relating
to our enhanced internal control measures); and
(vi) we had not encountered any material settlement issue after the cessation of the third-party
payment and as at the Latest Practicable Date.
Enhanced internal control measure
As advised by our Internal Control Consultant, we have placed the following internal control
measures in place to prevent the recurrence of third-party payments:
(i) disallowing payments from unknown bank accounts that are not pre-registered under the
name of the contractual party to our ticket bulk sales master agreements, as stipulated in
our internal policy, and communicating such a requirement to all of our ticket selling
distributors;
(ii) requiring all of our ticket-selling distributors to provide the details of their active corporate
bank accounts as soon as ticket bulk sales master agreements are entered into.Any updates
to the bank accounts details should be communicated by the said parties to us immediately
for our accurate and updated records. Each ticket selling distributor can provide us with
more than one corporate bank account, while all bank accounts should be registered in our
internal register under the name of the contractual party to our ticket bulk sales master
agreements. Only a contractual party to our ticket bulk sales master agreement with
registered corporate bank account can make payments to us. The said register should be
maintained from time to time to reflect accurate and updated information; and
(iii) our Directors have designated the finance department to thoroughly check and monitor all
payment details, including the name and bank account number of each payor, when
payments from ticket selling distributors are received. Sales department personnel will, in
parallel, check the payment details upon each payment receipt from our ticket selling
distributors. The said department, together with the responsible finance department
personnel, will jointly sign on the supporting document of payment as evidence of
inspection. If a payment is red-flagged as coming from an unregistered bank account, it will
not be accepted in our ticket management system and will be returned to the respective
payor. The said verification process should be conducted to ensure that payments are not
made from unregistered bank accounts. While the aforesaid enhanced procedures disallow
unauthorised parties to conduct payment to us, our chief financial officer and finance
manager will review the supporting documents of payments received at the end of each
month. In addition, they have been designated to conduct monthly checks with ticket
selling distributors to ensure that the aforesaid enhanced procedures have been strictly and
effectively adhered to.

We have accumulated extensive practical experience since the debut of our Impression —

to accurately identify core needs and strategic directions when innovating and enhancing the show’s
appeal.
According to industry practice, the party responsible for carrying out daily operations of the
show usually also oversees directing and innovation efforts, as it has first-hand and a more direct
understanding of the show’s performance, audience feedback, and market trends. As the operating
party, we are empowered to lead and implement updates and improvements to the Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show. According to Frost & Sullivan, this approach aligns with industry
standards and enables us to respond effectively to market demands. Moreover, according to the
contractual terms between our Company and Impression Art Development, we are entitled to
independently fine-tune the show based on our own improvement ideas. See “Industry Overview —

a show at different phases.

Seasonality
Our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is subject to seasonality of the tourism market,
statutory holidays and festivals throughout the year. The revenue from our Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show may demonstrate an obvious seasonality depending on the demand for our show tickets.
Historically and during the Track Record Period, peak seasons generally represented:
• Major holidays such as May Day Holiday (International Labour Holiday) often
characterised by increased number of travellers due to the holiday break; Chinese National
Holiday (October Golden Week Holiday) attracting large crowds of travellers as families
and tourists taking advantage of an extended break; and Spring Festival (Chinese Lunar
New Year).
• School breaks such as summer holidays which record a rise in family travel, contributing
to increased tourist activities.

The performance of our show may be suspended in the event of bad or extreme weather
conditions. Given that our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show is conducted outdoors, we
prioritise the safety of our audience and performers. Our management team has equipped themselves
with basic knowledge of satellite and radar meteorological imagery. In anticipation of a potential bad
or extreme weather condition in Mount Wuyi, they maintain close communications with the local
meteorological and hydrological authorities and discuss with the performance manager of the show,
and accordingly make decisions with respect to the performance schedules. Any suspension of
performances will be documented and announced to our audience in an immediate manner.
In the event of an actual bad or extreme weather condition preventing our performance, we will
inform our ticket selling distributors and a performance cancellation notice will be issued. Ticket
refund requests will subsequently be processed. If the performance is in progress when there is a
sudden bad or extreme weather condition, an audio announcement will be made in the auditorium to
inform our audience of the immediate cancellation of our performance. Ticket refund requests will be
processed for those who opt not to watch a rescheduled show. We may also arrange additional
performances for those who opt to re-attend the show.

BUSINESS
Moonlight Over Mount Wuyi
In recent years, we have actively pursued new development opportunities in the tourism scenery
performance market. In September 2024, Moonlight Wuyi was incorporated for the purpose of
curating and performing a new show, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi, which is performed in an indoor
theatre in Mount Wuyi. Through a public bidding process, Moonlight Wuyi engaged a directorial
team, which provided directorial services to Moonlight Wuyi. As at the Latest Practicable Date,
Moonlight Wuyi is owned as to 40.0% by our Company, 25% by Moonlight Wuyi (Beijing) Cultural
Media Co., Ltd (月映武夷(北京)文化傳媒有限公司), and 35% by Fujian Wuyi Tourism Group (which
holds 33.7% equity interest in Mount Wuyi Cultural Tourism, one of our Controlling Shareholders
(with 68.8% shareholding in our Company)). The ultimate beneficial owner of Fujian Wuyi Tourism
Group is Nanping SASAC. Ms. Xu Zhoumei, our non-executive Director, holds the directorship of
Fujian Wuyi Tourism Group. Save for the aforesaid relationship, none of our other Directors, senior
management and their close associates are interested in Fujian Wuyi Tourism Group. As Fujian Wuyi
Tourism Group is principally engaged in tourism-related investment, Fujian Wuyi Tourism Group and
our Company decided to jointly incorporate a company, aiming to achieve mutual benefits through
resource integration and to further enhance the development of the local cultural tourism industry in
Mount Wuyi City.
Moonlight over Mount Wuyi was initially funded by the paid up capital of Moonlight Wuyi. As
at the Latest Practicable Date, we had fully paid up RMB80.0 million for the registered capital of
Moonlight Wuyi. The debut of this new show took place on 17 April 2025, followed by the premiere
of the show to the public on 1 May 2025. By leveraging on our prior success of the Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show, Moonlight over MountWuyi focuses on the core philosophies of “investing
things to attain knowledge” (格物致知) and “attaining the knowledge of the goods”（致良知）, which
embody the Zhuzi culture of Mount Wuyi (武夷山朱子文化), distinguishing it as an indoor live show
from the existing Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show.
Based on the script provided by the aforementioned directorial team, Moonlight over Mount
Wuyi begins with an art performance under a bright moon, setting the stage for the cultural backdrop
of Mount Wuyi. The show unfolds through a structured narrative that highlights Zhu Xi (朱熹)’s
childhood curiosity about the heavens, his journeys through famous mountains and rivers and his
philosophy’s core ideas and influences, culminating in a reflection on his academic achievements
through exchanges with other scholars. The epilogue uses a pond as a symbol of the enduring nature
of Chinese civilisation, emphasising the importance of protecting cultural heritage. The performance
will intricately weave profound philosophy into a poetic narrative, showcasing unique Eastern
aesthetic concepts. Utilising modern technology, the show creates an immersive experience that
transports the audience to the cultural atmosphere of the Song Dynasty. Furthermore, the show
innovatively integrates Zhuzi culture, exploring its philosophical significance and societal value,
while advocating for the preservation of traditional culture alongside modern innovation. The
performance also emphasises the unique ecological and cultural resources of Mount Wuyi, calling on
society to actively engage in protecting these invaluable heritages.
− 198 −

=== PAGE 207 ===
BUSINESS
Performance
With the premiere of the show on 1 May 2025, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi has become another
highlight of Fujian Province’s cultural tourism industry. The performance occurs in a specially
designed indoor theatre, with each performance lasting approximately 70 minutes. A dedicated team
of more than 120 professional performers brings the production to life, incorporating a variety of art
forms, including dance, music, drama, martial arts and multimedia interaction. Through its highly
artistic choreography, audiences of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi experience the revival of the
millennia of history and humanistic spirit of Mount Wuyi, showcasing its unique natural beauty and
cultural richness. The show applies technology by introduction of a three-dimensional water scenery
of 8,225 m3. The performance stage is featured as the “Largest Single Structure Indoor Water Curtain
Stage”, which has been endorsed by the World Record Certification Limited on 1 May 2025. The
theatre of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi is located in an area within Mount Wuyi City which is
approximately 3.3km (or a 10 minutes drive) from the auditorium of Impression — Dahongpao
Scenery Show.
Since 1 May 2025 and up to the Latest Practicable Date, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi has been
performed more than 329 times and more than 91,000 audience attended the show since its launch in
May 2025. With its successful launch, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi is gradually becoming an integral
part of the cultural tourism industry in Mount Wuyi and Fujian Province, while actively contributing
to the promotion of traditional Chinese culture.
Additionally, with its immersive live performance and world-class stage technology, Moonlight
over Mount Wuyi has become a media sensation following its premiere on 1 May 2025. On 3 May
2025, CCTV’s Chinese International Channel (央視中文國際頻道) featured the performance stage of
the show in various television programmes including Today’s Global (今日環球) and China News
(中國新聞). On 5 May 2025, News Channel (新聞直播間) highlighted Moonlight over Mount Wuyi as
a brand new cultural tourism experience that ignites the holiday economy in China.

Latest Practicable Date, the maximum number of the performances of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi
was two during a day. At maximum capacity and on a fully packed schedule, the maximum number
of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi performances that can be performed per day is six.

Obtaining the Leasing Right of the Theatre
Moonlight over Mount Wuyi is performed indoors at a theatre, located in the Mount Wuyi Resort
Area. The theatre is owned by Mount Wuyi Tourism Cultural Investment. Mount Wuyi Tourism
Cultural Investment is wholly owned by Mount Wuyi City Construction Group Company Limited (武
夷山城市建設投資集團有限公司), which is a fellow subsidiary under the control of Mount Wuyi
SAOSC. Two of our Controlling Shareholders, namely MountWuyi CulturalTourism and MountWuyi
Tourism Resort Development are also the fellow subsidiaries under the control of Mount Wuyi
SAOSC. The indoor theatre has a total capacity of 1,971 audience seats, of which 1,175 are regular
seats, and 796 are VIP seats.
On 28April 2025, we entered into a lease agreement with Mount Wuyi City Construction Group
Company Limited, with a term of 20 years. According to the lease agreement, the annual leasing fee
for us to use the theatre is 10.0% of the operating income from the performance of Moonlight over
Mount Wuyi (representing the revenue from sales of tickets), or RMB5.0 million, whichever is higher.

Settlement method Each ticket selling distributor will be issued a user account
with a specific login username and password under our ticket
management system, through which the ticket selling
distributor shall place the purchase orders and make
prepayments to us prior to our issuance of tickets.
Prepayments are typically made via bank transfer, or taken by
POS portable machine. Prepayments will thereafter be
recorded on the ticket management system.
Credit term Our ticket selling distributors purchase our show tickets
through their prepayments to our Company, deduction of
which will occur upon our issuance of show tickets to them.
Performance deposit As a prerequisite for a ticket selling distributor to be formally
engaged by us, it is obliged to pay a fixed amount (with a
minimum of RMB10,000) as performance deposit, which
serves as a minimum guarantee of income for us. Such fixed
amount varies for each ticket selling distributor, which is
determined with reference to the sales volume target agreed
in the relevant ticket bulk sales master agreement. The
performance deposit must be paid within three business days
from the date of the ticket bulk sales master agreement.
The performance deposit may be refunded in part or in full or
used as prepayment for tickets sold, depending on how much
of the sales volume target is achieved, as specified in the
agreement. However, if the ticket selling distributor fails to
achieve 50% of its sales volume target, none of the
performance deposit may be refunded.
Credit assessment score Each ticket selling distributor is allocated a credit assessment
score as a means for us to keep track of the distributor’s
compliance with our ticket selling requirements. If we
become aware that the ticket selling distributor violated our
prescribed policy for sale of tickets (including onwards sale
of our tickets at a price lower than the prescribed price), a
penalty will be imposed (by way of confiscation of a certain
amount of the quality deposit according to specific
circumstances specified in the agreement) and the credit
assessment score may be deducted.
If the ticket selling distributor’s annual credit assessment
score falls below 80 out of 100, we may terminate the
bilateral ticket bulk sales master agreement, and the
distributor will be disqualified from being our ticket selling
distributor in the following year.

BUSINESS
Quality deposit Quality deposit serves as an incentive for the ticket selling
distributors to achieve higher sales volume, and also as a
deterrent in respect of violation by ticket selling distributors
of our prescribed policy for sale of tickets. Upon the sale of
each ticket, the ticket selling distributor shall pay an extra fee

ticket sold, and shall be settled at the same time along with

number of tickets sold by the ticket selling distributor during
the term of the agreement (whereby a higher sales volume
will result in a higher refundable amount). However, if the
ticket selling distributor fails to achieve 70% of its sales
volume target, none of the quality deposit may be refunded.
Also, as mentioned above, if we become aware that the ticket
selling distributor violated our prescribed policy for sale of
tickets, a certain amount of the quality deposit may be
confiscated by us. Any refundable amount of quality deposit
shall be settled after we complete the audit of the number of
tickets sold by each of the ticket selling distributors at the
end of the term.
Early termination right We have the right to terminate a bilateral ticket bulk sales
master agreement upon any of the following
i) the ticket selling distributor’s annual credit assessment
score is lower than 80 out of 100 as mentioned above;
ii) the ticket selling distributor failed to pay the

stipulated in the relevant ticket bulk sales master
agreements; and
iii) the ticket selling distributor breached the terms of the

penalised by relevant authorities. In such case, no
performance deposit or quality deposit shall be
refundable.
Refund of tickets Unless due to force majeure events, such as adverse weather
or special seating arrangements, we are not obligated to

Pricing
As confirmed by our PRC LegalAdvisers, the pricing of sales of show tickets for our Moonlight
over Mount Wuyi is market-based.
Tickets for our Moonlight over Mount Wuyi consist of two types: (i) tickets for regular seats,
and (ii) tickets for VIP seats (which are further divided into various VIP categories). Since the
premiere of the show on 1 May 2025 and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we sold more than 91,500
show tickets. We require full payment before we issue show tickets to our audience and the ticket
selling distributors.
As at the Latest Practicable Date, tickets for regular seats are priced at RMB238, and VIP seats
are priced at a range from RMB268 to RMB588. These are direct sales price where tickets are sold
directly to our audience at our ticket selling points. In certain occasions, we also sell group tickets
to trade unions at a discounted price of RMB119 for regular seats and/or at other special promotional
deals. To strengthen the positioning of our Moonlight over Mount Wuyi as a promotion of traditional
Chinese philosophy and culture, we also offer concession tickets at RMB89 for students or schools.
For sales to ticket selling distributors, the settlement price offered to our ticket selling
distributors are lower than the direct sales prices offered to our audience, as we can benefit from
advantages of bulk sales. The ticket price at which the ticket selling distributors can sell onwards to
end customers are governed by terms stipulated in the relevant bilateral ticket sales agreement signed
with us.
During the six months ended 30 June 2025, to the best knowledge of our Directors, no tickets
of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi were sold by our ticket selling distributors at a price below the
minimum retail price as stipulated in the relevant ticket sales agreements. Typically, we monitor the
ticket price through market investigation by our sales personnel. Our sales personnel also conduct
sample checks on various online platforms to monitor the actual selling price of tickets sold by the
ticket selling distributors. We also adopt a quota system which limits the total number of tickets that
can be requested by the ticket selling distributors under the relevant ticket sales agreements. The
number of tickets that can be requested ranges from 20 to 50 on a daily basis. Once the quota is
reached, the ticket selling distributors may opt to purchase show tickets from other ticket selling
distributors. Nonetheless, the ticket selling distributors may purchase additional show tickets after
12:00 pm of that day, if there is availability. Each of our show tickets is issued for a specific
performance on the indicated date. If any audience holding a show ticket cannot attend due to personal
reasons, we do not allow refunds in normal circumstances unless due to force majeure events such as
bad weather conditions. In light of the above, our Directors are of the view that we have adopted
effective measures to reduce the risk of cannibalisation.

the public’s awareness of our show and generate noise in marketing, as part of the process of building
up popularity and reputation of the show.
