BOARD DIVERSITY POLICY
We are committed to promoting the culture of diversity in our Company. We have strived to
promote diversity to the extent practicable by taking into consideration a number of factors in our
corporate governance structure.
We have adopted a board diversity policy (the “Board Diversity Policy”) to enhance the
effectiveness of our Board and to maintain a high standard of corporate governance. Pursuant to our
Board Diversity Policy, in reviewing and assessing suitable candidates to serve as a Director, the
nomination committee will consider a range of diversity perspectives with reference to our Company’s
business model and specific needs, including but not limited to gender, age, language, cultural and
educational background, professional qualifications, skills, knowledge, industry and regional
experience and/or length of service. Our Directors have a balanced mixed of knowledge and skills,
including but not limited to overall business management, finance and accounting and marketing.
They obtained degrees in various majors including but not limited to accounting, law, tourism and
business administration. Furthermore, our Board has a relatively wide range of ages, ranging from 47
years old to 57 years old with experience from different industries, sectors and genders.
We will continue to take steps to promote gender diversity at all levels of our Company,
including but not limited to our Board and the senior management levels. We will encourage our
incumbent Board members to recommend female candidate directors and take other actions to help
achieve greater board diversity, for example inviting some of our outstanding female staff at mid to
senior level to attend and observe Board meetings. This will allow our Board to understand more
− 302 −

=== PAGE 311 ===
DIRECTORS AND SENIOR MANAGEMENT
about these potential female candidates before they are nominated to our Board and provide
opportunities for potential female candidates to prepare themselves for director duties. We will also
continue to ensure that there is gender diversity when recruiting staff at mid to senior level so that
we will have a pipeline of female senior management and potential successors to our Board in due
time to ensure gender diversity of our Board. Our Group will continue to emphasise training of female
talent and providing long-term development opportunities for our female staff including but not
limited to business operation, management, accounting and finance, legal and compliance matters.As
such, we are of the view that our Board will be offered chances to identify competent female staff at
mid to senior level to be nominated as a Director in future with a pipeline of female candidates.
We are committed to adopting a similar approach to promote diversity within management
(including but not limited to the senior management) of our Company to enhance the effectiveness of
corporate governance of our Company as a whole.
Upon Listing, our Board comprises six male members and two female members. Our Nomination
Committee is responsible for ensuring the diversity of our Board members. After Listing, our
Nomination Committee will review the board diversity policy from time to time, develop and review
measurable objectives for implementing the policy, and monitor the progress on achieving these
measurable objectives to ensure its continued effectiveness. We will disclose in our corporate
governance report about the implementation of the board diversity policy on an annual basis.
MANAGEMENT PRESENCE
Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules provides that an applicant applying for a primary listing on the
Stock Exchange must have a sufficient management presence in Hong Kong. This will normally mean
that at least two of its executive directors must be ordinary resident in Hong Kong. We do not have
sufficient management presence in Hong Kong for the purposes of Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules.
Accordingly, we have applied to the Stock Exchange for, and the Stock Exchange has agreed to grant,
a waiver from strict compliance with Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules. See “Waivers from Strict
Compliance with the Listing Rules — Waiver in respect of Management Presence in Hong Kong” in
this prospectus for details.

and 14Aof the Listing Rules is contemplated, including share issues and share repurchases;

Stock Exchange. The compliance adviser will also inform our Company of any new or amended law,
regulation or code in Hong Kong applicable to us, and advise us on the continuing requirements under

RANKING
Upon completion of the Global Offering (assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised),
our Company would have 108,070,000 Unlisted Shares and 36,100,000 H Shares. The Unlisted Shares
which are currently not listed or traded on any stock exchange or authorised trading facility (other
than quoted on NEEQ). Both Unlisted Shares and H Shares are ordinary shares in the share capital
of our Company and are regarded as the same class of Shares.
Apart from certain qualified domestic institutional investors in the PRC, certain qualified PRC
investors under the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock
Connect, and other persons who are entitled to hold our H Shares pursuant to relevant PRC laws and
regulations or upon approvals of any competent authorities, H Shares generally cannot be subscribed
for by or traded among legal and natural persons of the PRC.
Unlisted Shares and H Shares will rank pari passu with each other in all other respects and, in
particular, will rank equally for all dividends or distributions declared, paid or made after the date of
this prospectus. All dividends in respect of the H Shares are to be paid by us in Hong Kong dollars
or in the form of H Shares.

OVERVIEW
We are a state-owned cultural tourism service provider headquartered in Mount Wuyi, Fujian
Province.According to Frost & Sullivan, we ranked the eighth in terms of sales revenue generated by
cultural tourism performance programs in the cultural tourism performance market in China in 2024.
Our primary focus has been our signature show, the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, which
is the first large-scale outdoor scenic performance in Fujian Province according to Frost & Sullivan,
and has been the principal generator of our revenue historically and during the Track Record Period.
As an expansion of our performance portfolio to cater to wider tourist preferences, we launched a new
show, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi 《( 月映武夷》). The debut of this new show took place on 17April
2025, followed by the premiere of the show to the public on 1 May 2025. In addition to our two
performance shows, we have been strategically developing our Impression Cultural Tourism Town
since 2019. We also expanded our business portfolio to include a Chatang hotel within the national
tourist resort area of Mount Wuyi since 2020.
Leveraging the rich tourism heritage and the unparalleled Dahongpao tea culture of MountWuyi,
we have established ourselves as a cultural tourism service provider in Fujian Province.We are deeply
rooted in, and committed to the local cultural tourism market and remain focused on unlocking the
tourism potential of MountWuyi by creating synergies from our diverse offerings. For the years ended
31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended 30 June 2024 and 2025, our total
revenue amounted to approximately RMB63.0 million, RMB143.9 million, RMB137.2 million,
RMB51.5 million and RMB55.9 million, respectively.

KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our results of operations and financial position have been and will continue to be affected by
a number of factors, including those set out in “Risk Factors” in this prospectus and those discussed
below:
Our ability to attract travellers to Mount Wuyi, where our business operations are concentrated,
and adjust to the tastes and preferences of travellers
The financial performance of our Group is significantly influenced by our continued ability to
attract travellers to Mount Wuyi and to respond to the evolving tastes and preferences of travellers.
UNESCO-recognised Mount Wuyi is renowned for its natural beauty, cultural heritage, and unique
attractions. Effectively highlighting these qualities through our marketing efforts is essential for
drawing diverse tourist demographics. Seasonal promotions and targeted campaigns can enhance our
visibility and broaden our audience. Understanding tourist preferences is crucial as consumer interests
increasingly shift toward experiential travel. It remains important that we adapt our service offerings
to meet these expectations by providing immersive cultural experiences, sustainable tourism options,
and personalised services that resonate with modern tourists. Regular market research and customer
feedback mechanisms will help us identify and respond to these trends effectively. It is therefore
imperative that we maintain our competitiveness and the appeal of each of our business segments,
being shows and performance services, Impression CulturalTourismTown business and Chatang hotel
business.
Our cultural tourism business operates exclusively in Fujian Province, where all of our business
activities are centralised. This geographic concentration allows us to focus our efforts on enhancing
our position as a cultural tourism service provider in Fujian Province. However, it also exposes us to
various risks associated with regional economic fluctuations, environmental challenges, and shifts in
local regulations. For instance, economic downturns in China could result in reduced consumer
spending on leisure activities, directly impacting our visitor numbers. Additionally, environmental
factors such as natural disasters or the effects of climate change may disrupt access to key attractions
such as Mount Wuyi, deterring potential tourists. Furthermore, changes in local regulations, whether
related to cultural tourism, environmental protection, or business operations, could introduce new
challenges to our business model. Any adverse developments in the tourism scenery performance
market or cultural tourism performance market could significantly affect our operations and lead to
a decline in tourist attendance, ultimately affecting our financial performance.

Impact of transportation disruptions on financial performance
Any disruption to the schedule or increase in the price of flights and trains to and from Mount
Wuyi could significantly reduce the demand for our service offerings to tourists. Such disruptions may
discourage potential visitors from traveling, which would adversely affect our business operations,
results, and overall financial condition. Specifically, rising transportation costs can lead to decreased
consumer spending on leisure activities, as tourists may prioritise essential expenses over optional
travel. Furthermore, delays or cancellations in transportation services could deter tourists from
planning trips to our destination. These transportation-related issues could potentially undermine our
ability to attract and retain visitors, ultimately impacting our revenue generation and long-term
sustainability.
Seasonal fluctuations in terms of the financial performance of our shows
The financial performance of our shows, namely, the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show
and Moonlight over Mount Wuyi are affected by seasonal fluctuations. Throughout the Track Record
Period, peak seasons primarily coincided with major holidays and school vacations.As a result, sales
and operating results for a specific period may not accurately represent our overall results for the
entire year or future periods. Additionally, our interim results might not proportionally reflect our
annual performance. For a detailed explanation of the implications of seasonality, including a monthly
revenue breakdown during the Track Record Period for a quantitative analysis, see “Business —
Shows and Performance Services — Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show — Seasonality” and
“Business — Shows and Performance Services — Moonlight Over MountWuyi — Seasonality” in this
prospectus.
Dependence on the reputation of our brandname “Impression — Dahongpao”
We depend on the strong reputation of “Impression — Dahongpao” to curate and perform our
signature show, which is vital for attracting tourists and generating revenue. This established brand
recognition not only benefits our show but also influences our other business segments, including our
Impression Cultural Tourism Town business and Chatang hotel business. Consequently, any incidents
or adverse publicity related to our brandname could significantly harm our overall reputation.
Negative media coverage, customer complaints, or operational failures can lead to diminished public
perception of our show and may even extend to our entire suite of cultural tourism services. Such
reputational damage may result in decreased attendance, lower ticket sales, and an overall decline in
profitability. Therefore, maintaining a positive reputation is essential for our success. Any negativity
to our brand name could have lasting effects on our business operations and financial performance,
underscoring the importance of proactive reputation management.
Business expansions with enlarged live show portfolio and cultural tourism service portfolio
The development and expansion of our live shows, along with our broader initiatives in the
cultural tourism industry and Chatang hotel business, may present new challenges that we are not fully
equipped to handle. As we seek to enhance our service offerings and capture a larger market share,
we face several potential obstacles that could impact our operations and financial performance.
Expansion of our live show portfolio, further development of our Impression Cultural Tourism Town
business and entering into the hotel sector introduces greater operational complexity. Managing

multiple performance venues and coordinating diverse tourist attractions requires a level of expertise
and resources that may stretch our current capabilities. If we fail to effectively navigate these
complexities, it may be possible that we risk operational inefficiencies that could negatively affect the
guest experience. Additionally, the lack of experience in these new areas may hinder our ability to
make informed strategic decisions. Without the necessary background in hospitality management or
the broader cultural tourism landscape, we may encounter difficulties in adapting our business model
to meet evolving market demands. Furthermore, as we expand, we will inevitably face increased
competition from established players in the cultural tourism industry. Competing with other cultural
tourism service providers with more experience and established customer bases can be particularly
challenging. If we are unable to differentiate our offerings, effectively market our brandname, or fail
to equip ourselves with sufficient human resources, we may struggle to attract customers and achieve
our growth objectives.
Our overall financial results depend on reversing the net loss position of our Chatang hotel
business
Our financial performance is significantly influenced by our ability to reverse the net loss
position of our Chatang hotel business. Our Chatang hotel opened in 2021 and has a history of
incurring gross losses. For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months
ended 30 June 2024 and 2025, our Chatang hotel recorded gross losses of approximately RMB6.5
million, RMB5.5 million, RMB6.2 million, RMB3.1 million and RMB2.7 million, respectively.
We should remain dedicated to implementing strategies specifically designed to reverse the net
loss position of our Chatang hotel. By improving operational efficiency and attracting a broader
clientele, we believe we can turn this business around. Our ability to successfully addressing the
challenges our Chatang hotel encounters will have a positive impact on our overall business and
financial results. Nonetheless, there is no guarantee that our efforts to improve operational efficiency
and attract a wider clientele will lead to sustained profitability. Various external factors, such as
intense market competition in the hotel business sector in Mount Wuyi City, shifts in guest
preferences, economic downturns and operational challenges, could adversely impact our financial
performance.
Services and customer mix
During the Track Record Period, the majority of our revenue was derived from our shows and
performance services. During the same period, we also generated revenue from our Impression
Cultural Tourism Town business and Chatang hotel business. In respect of our shows, customers were
primarily ticket selling distributors which conduct onward sales of tickets, and audience who directly
purchased our show tickets through our ticket selling points. Customers also included corporate
customers which requested for customised performances. Typically, these corporate customers
engaged us to perform at their special corporate events, such as team-building activities and annual
meetings. During the Track Record Period, our ticket selling distributors contributed approximately
91.9%, 92.6%, 92.3% and 89.6% of the revenue for the provision of our shows. Accordingly, it
remains crucial that we maintain good relationships with our ticket selling distributors who are able
to assist us in securing broad end customer base, being the audience of our signature show. In respect
of our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business and the Chatang hotel business, customers were
primarily travellers to Mount Wuyi.

Impact of COVID-19 before policy relaxation
Before the relaxation of COVID-19 restrictions, our combined cultural tourism business
experienced significant disruptions in 2022. The pandemic led to a decline in tourist numbers
primarily because travel restrictions, health protocols, and safety concerns deterred the public from
engaging in leisure activities. During this period, our operations were adversely affected by a decrease
in our total number of performances of our show, reduced attendance at our Impression Cultural
Tourism Town and a decrease in guests at our Chatang hotel, resulting in lower revenue and
profitability. Many events were postponed or cancelled, and our ability to market and promote our
service offerings was severely limited.
MATERIAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ESTIMATES
We have identified certain accounting policies that are most significant to the preparation of our
historical financial information. Some of our material accounting policies involve subjective
assumptions and estimates, as well as complex judgements by our management relating to accounting
items. Our Group makes estimates and assumptions concerning the future. Estimates and judgements
are continuously evaluated and are based on historical experience and other factors, including
expectations of future events that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. Set out below
are accounting policies which we believe are of critical importance to us or involve the most
significant estimates, assumptions and judgments used in the preparation of our financial statements.
Our material accounting policies, estimates, assumptions and judgments, which are important for
understanding our financial condition and results of operations, are set out in further detail in notes
2, 3.1 and 3.2 in Appendix I to this prospectus.
Revenue Recognition
We adopted HKFRS 15, which refers to “Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard 15” aligning
with the International Financial Reporting Standard 15, focusing on revenue recognition. HKFRS 15
provides guidelines on how and when to recognise revenue from contracts with customers, ensuring
that revenue reflects the transfer of services to customers at an amount that reflects the consideration
expected in exchange.
Key principles of HKFRS 15 include:
• Identifying Contracts: Recognising revenue only when there is a contract with
enforceable rights and obligations.
• Performance Obligations: Identifying distinct goods or services within the contract.
• Transaction Price: Determining the transaction price, including variable consideration,
and allocating it to the performance obligations.
• Recognition of Revenue: Recognising revenue when performance obligations are satisfied.
− 314 −

=== PAGE 323 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
Shows and performance services
Revenue from the provision of our two performance shows, namely the Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show and Moonlight over Mount Wuyi were recognised at a point in time when
the performance is completed and our Group has a present right to payment and the collection of the
consideration is probable. This was usually taken at the time when the services were rendered. The
completion of services generally occurred upon completion of performance of the shows. In respect
of sales of tickets, we recognise revenue from sales of tickets for our performance shows irrespective
of attendance of audience at our auditorium, as well as no-show situations. That said, we are not
obligated to refund payments for tickets to our audience who opted not to attend the shows. It is
possible that the ticket issuance rate of our performance shows may not accurately reflect our actual
attendance situation. In respect of special event performances, revenue was recognised after
completion of the performances.
Impression Cultural Tourism Town business
Revenue from our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business included a variety of cultural
tourism service offerings provided in the town by us and by third parties who operate their business
in the town. Those services, except rental income, was recognised at a point in time when the service
is rendered; and our Group has present rights to payment and the collection of the consideration is
probable.This is usually taken at the time when the services are rendered. Rental income is recognised
on a straight-line basis over the term of the relevant lease.
Chatang hotel business
During the Track Record Period, we also generated revenue from our Chatang hotel business,
including (i) accommodation fees from room nights sold to room guests, which were recognised over
time when the accommodation services were rendered, and (ii) fees from catering, Chatang and
ancillary services, which were recognised at the point in time when the meal and ancillary services
were provided. We control the specified services before we transfer the services to our customers
(representing the room guests and travellers to Mount Wuyi) after taking into account that we are
primarily responsible for discharging our contractual commitment under the service terms by
providing the required services to our customers.When we satisfy the service performance obligation,
we recognise the revenue from such services in the gross amount of consideration, to which we are
entitled under the service terms.
Current Income Tax
Our Group is subject to Enterprise Income Tax (“EIT”) in China, which requires significant
judgment in determining the appropriate provision for EIT. During the normal course of our business,
there are various transactions and calculations where the ultimate tax determination may be uncertain.
If the final tax outcomes differ from the amounts initially recorded, these differences will affect both
our current income tax and deferred tax provisions in the period when the determinations are made.
This inherent uncertainty underscores the importance of our accounting policies and estimates related
to income tax, which are critical for accurately reflecting our financial position and performance.

Cultural Tourism Town.

cooperating partners for our service offerings, such as Thai Natural.

offerings, such as water, props and costumes.

Gross profit of our shows and performance services
For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended 30 June 2024
and 2025, gross profit for the shows and performance services was approximately RMB22.0 million,
RMB86.5 million, RMB79.3 million, RMB27.9 million and RMB25.6 million, respectively. For the
same years/period, the gross profit margin of our shows and performance services was approximately
38.0%, 63.4%, 61.0%, 58.1% and 49.3%, respectively.
For the year ended 31 December 2023, the gross profit margin of our shows and performance
services segment significantly increased by approximately 25.4 percentage points compared with that
of for the year ended 31 December 2022. The main reason was attributable to an increase in the
revenue generated from sales of tickets of Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, which increased
by RMB78.4 million, or approximately 135.4% during the year. The corresponding cost of sales
increased by approximately RMB13.9 million, or approximately 38.8% during the year. The cost of
sales consisted of both fixed costs and variable costs. Fixed costs mainly included depreciation of
assets and salaries of our employees. Fixed costs increased by approximately RMB1.4 million during
the year, because of the renovation works we undertook in 2023. Variable costs mainly included
directorial royalty service expenses and bonus of our employees. Variable costs increased by
approximately RMB12.5 million during the year, because bonus of our employees and salaries of
part-time performance team members increased as a result of an increase in the number of shows
performed during the year. That said, in respect of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show and
performance services, the growth rate of cost of sales was slower than the growth rate of revenue in
2023. During the year, cost of sales consisted of approximately 47.4% of fixed costs and
approximately 52.6% of variable costs. Consequently, the impact of the increase in variable costs was
mitigated by the larger portion of fixed costs following the increase in revenue.
For the year ended 31 December 2024, the gross profit margin of our shows and performance
services segment decreased by approximately 2.4 percentage points compared with that for the year
ended 31 December 2023. The main reason was attributable to a decrease in revenue generated from
sales of tickets of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, which decreased by approximately
RMB6.4 million, or approximately 4.7% during the year. Nonetheless, the corresponding cost of sales
increased by approximately RMB0.9 million, or approximately 1.7% during the year. Fixed costs
increased by approximately RMB1.8 million because of an increase in the salaries of our employees,
while variable costs decreased by approximately RMB0.9 million. That said, in respect of our shows
and performance services, the increase in cost of sales was slightly slower than the decrease in
revenue, comprising approximately 49.9% of fixed costs and approximately 50.1% of variable costs.
Consequently, the significant portion of fixed costs offset the impact of the decrease in variable costs
following the decrease in revenue in 2024.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
For the six months ended 30 June 2025, the gross profit margin for our shows and performance
services segment decreased by approximately 8.8 percentage points compared with that for the six
months ended 30 June 2024. This is despite stable results from our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery
Show, which recorded a gross profit margin of 55.3% during the six months ended 30 June 2025, as
compared to a gross profit margin of 58.1% during the corresponding period in 2024. Our overall
decrease in gross profit margin of this segment was mainly affected by the gross loss position of
approximately RMB1.8 million and gross loss margin of approximately 76.7% of our Moonlight over
Mount Wuyi, which launched in May 2025. Since this new show was still in early start-up stage, its
revenue generated was insufficient to cover its cost of sales. During the six months ended 30 June
2025, Moonlight over Mount Wuyi incurred cost of sales of approximately RMB4.2 million, and
generated revenue of approximately RMB2.4 million. Moreover, we have made an upward
adjustments to our frontline employees’ wages since September 2024, which increased the cost of
sales by approximately RMB2.4 million for the six months ended 30 June 2025. Therefore, despite an
increase in revenue generated from the shows and performance services of approximately RMB4.0
million compared with the same period in 2024, the corresponding gross profit margin decreased.

Gross loss of our Chatang Hotel Business
For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended 30 June 2024
and 2025, gross loss of our Chatang hotel business was approximately RMB6.5 million, RMB5.5
million, RMB6.2 million, RMB3.1 million and RMB2.7 million , respectively. For the same
years/periods, the gross loss margin of our Chatang hotel business was approximately 313.7%,
140.9%, 162.2%, 164.8% and 135.2%, respectively.
Our Chatang hotel opened in 2021 amid the COVID-19 pandemic, which proved to be
particularly bad timing, as the pandemic severely disrupted the hospitality, accommodation and
tourism industries till 2023. From 2021 to 2022, the number of travellers visiting Mount Wuyi
dropped by approximately 50.0% according to the local government’s announcement, leading to a
market decline in travel and accommodation demand, due to the enhanced travel restrictions. As a
result, we recorded a low guest room occupancy rate of our Chatang hotel in 2022. Although the
average annual guest room occupancy rate of our Chatang Hotel increased steadily during the Track
Record Period, intensified competition in both the Mount Wuyi City local market and the wider hotel
− 326 −

=== PAGE 335 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
industry continued to exert pressure on our Chatang hotel business, resulting in a sustained gross loss
position. For the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six months ended 30 June
2025, the average annual guest room occupancy rate of our Chatang hotel was approximately 10.2%,
22.6%, 21.8% and 24.8%, respectively. The revenue generated from Chatang hotel business was
approximately RMB2.1 million, RMB3.9 million, RMB3.8 million, RMB1.9 million and RMB2.0
million for the corresponding years/period.
The gross loss margin of our Chatang hotel business improved from 164.8% as at 30 June 2024
to 135.2% as at 30 June 2025. This was primarily due to an adjustment of our revenue distribution
mechanism under the Chatang Management Arrangements upon its entering into the second phase in
January 2025, pursuant to which our management fee payable to Thai Natural has decreased. During
the first phase (1 October 2020 to 31 December 2024), we were obliged to pay to Thai Natural a
management fee representing 70% and 85% of the revenue recognised by Mount Wuyi Chatang Resort
in respect of room nights sold and Chatang services, as well as the provision of catering and ancillary
services, respectively. During the second phase (1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026), we are obliged
to pay to Thai Natural a management fee representing 50% of the revenue recognised by Mount Wuyi
Chatang Resort in respect of the same corresponding services. Therefore, the management fee payable
to Thai Natural decreased, which resulted in the cost of sales of our Chatang hotel business decreased
to approximately RMB4.6 million for the six months ended 30 June 2025 from approximately RMB5.0
million for the same period in 2024. For details of the key terms of the Chatang Management
Arrangements, please refer to the paragraph headed “Business — Chatang Hotel Business — Hotel
Management” in this prospectus.
According to Frost & Sullivan, as of January 2025, there were 800 registered lodging
establishments in Mount Wuyi City, including 218 hotels and 582 homestays. Accommodations
featuring hot spring services in Mount Wuyi City are dominated by homestays. Among these
accommodations, Mount Wuyi Wyndham Garden Hotel, which was opened in 2014, has an advantage
in the number of rooms. On the upstream side, our Chatang hotel had to deal with the competitive edge
of traditional hot spring hotel in group bookings, while on the downstream, our Chatang hotel faces
fierce competition from the local accommodation which offer relatively low prices.
In addition to the macro external environment, the operation of our Chatang hotel business
heavily relied upon online travel agencies as the primary source of our room guests, lacking
development of high-value guest segments such as business conferences and corporate events. The
limited guest portfolio restrained our revenue diversification from different customers. Moreover,
profitability of our Chatang hotel business is also subject to seasonality. November to March of each
year has been the off-peak season of our Chatang hotel business since its opening in 2021. During the
said off-season period, the guest room occupancy rate falls below 30.0%, affecting the overall
profitability of our Chatang hotel business.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
While we acknowledge the limits of our Chatang hotel business due to the aforesaid intensified
competition and fixed costs factors, we aim to launch various promotional activities to generate
synergies between our Moonlight over MountWuyi and our Chatang hotel, as the theatre of Moonlight
over Mount Wuyi is located close to our Chatang hotel. Since 2024, we have invested more resources
and increased our efforts in promoting the appeal of our Chatang hotel as an upscale family friendly
holiday destination on online platforms, through the word-of-mouth marketing of our staff of the
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show, and through our ticket selling distributors who had the first
chance dealing with the travellers to Mount Wuyi. Following the launch of our new show, Moonlight
over Mount Wuyi, which is expected to bring more foot traffic to nearby areas, we offered packaged
sales of show tickets together with Chatang hotel rooms. We believe we can improve the guest room
occupancy rate of our Chatang hotel and therefore improve the gross loss position of our Chatang
hotel business. Moreover, our Chatang hotel is located in an area where all buildings are of ancient
Chinese architecture, and the addition of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi as an attraction nearby elevates
the cultural atmosphere of the area, further enhancing its appeal to tourists who prefer to experience
the cultural aspect in their travels. We aim to feature our Chatang hotel as a Zhuzi culture-themed
hotel and host a series of cultural activities in the hotel. By showcasing the essence of Zhuzi culture,
we can provide guests with an immersive experience of this traditional culture, enhancing our hotel’s
cultural atmosphere and appeal. Moreover, based on the revenue distribution mechanism under the
Chatang Management Arrangements, since 1 January 2025, the management fee payable to Thai
Natural has been adjusted downwards. In light of this, we believe the gross loss position of our
Chatang hotel business can be further improved.
Based on the aforesaid measures and combining our breakeven analysis on our Chatang hotel
business, we expect to reverse the loss-making position of the segment by 2030.
Impairment assessment of Chatang hotel business
We have performed impairment assessment for Chatang hotel business. The recoverable amounts
of the cash-generating unit where Chatang hotel business belongs to are determined using valuation
method of income approach of discounted cash flows for value-in-use calculation. We, with the
assistance of an independent third-party valuer, prepared a cash flow forecast covering a five-year
period. Cash flows beyond the five-year period are extrapolated using the long-term growth rate. The
discount rate was derived from the weighted average cost of capital.

not yet settled the remaining RMB447,211 of such compensation.

As our Company and all of our operating subsidiaries are incorporated in China, we are subject
to EIT of the PRC on each of our Company and our subsidiaries’ taxable income in accordance with
the EIT Law. According to the EIT Law, a uniform 25% EIT rate is generally applicable to both
foreign-invested enterprises and domestic enterprises, except where a special preferential rate applies,
which does not apply to our Group. The EIT is calculated based on the entity’s global income as
determined under PRC tax laws and accounting standards.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had fulfilled all our
income tax obligations and have not had any unresolved income tax issues or disputes with the
relevant tax authorities.
Profit/(Loss) for the Year
As a result of the foregoing, for the years ended 31 December 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the six
months ended 30 June 2024 and 2025, our net profits/(losses) were approximately RMB(2.6) million,
RMB47.5 million, RMB42.8 million, RMB12.7 million and RMB6.8 million, respectively. For the
same years, our net profit/(loss) margins were approximately (4.1)%, 33.0%, 31.2%, 24.6% and
12.1%, respectively.
We improved our net loss position in 2022 to net profit position in 2023, primarily due to an
increase in our total revenue following the end of COVID-19. The lifting of COVID-19 restrictions
in December 2022 was the key contributing factor to the resurgence of broad tourism industry,
reflecting the release of pent-up demand in tourism that had been suppressed during the lockdown.
Similarly, our net profit decreased by approximately RMB4.7 million from 2023 to 2024, primarily
due to a decrease in revenue from our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show and performance
services, as (i) leisure spending activities, especially tourism spending, in 2024 was not as active as
that in the previous year after the release of the pent-up demand in 2023. 2023 recorded significant
improvement in tourist levels as COVID-19 officially came to an end. There was a notable increase
in consumer enthusiasm for non-essential spendings, particularly in the tourism sector. Following a
period of restrictions and limitations as a result of COVID-19, many individuals opted to seize the
travelling experiences they had previously missed; (ii) there was a longer closure of our Impression
— Dahongpao Scenery Show during the period between the start of the new year and the start of the
Spring Festival (Chinese Lunar New Year) holidays, which is the typical rest period for our
performers. In 2024, we closed for 35 days as the Spring Festival occurred in February 2024,
compared to our closure for 22 days in 2023 as the Spring Festival occurred in January 2023; and (iii)
bad weather conditions in June 2024 resulted in a drop in audience and even the temporary closure
of our performance stage and auditorium for our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show. For the six
months ended 30 June 2025, net profit of our Group was mainly impacted by the launch of our new
show Moonlight over MountWuyi in May 2025. Prior to its launch, we had to make significant capital
outlays and investment, such as equipment purchases and costs of performers who underwent training
and rehearsals, without any revenue generation from ticket sales. After its launch, as the show was
still in its early start-up stage, we had to carry out various marketing deals to promote the show and
attract audience, which led to higher marketing expenses and at times resulted in us selling tickets at
highly discounted prices or offering complimentary tickets as part of our marketing campaign.
− 336 −

=== PAGE 345 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
We have taken, and plan to take, a series of measures to improve our financial performance. Such
measures include: (i) in respect of Moonlight over Mount Wuyi, increasing marketing efforts to trade
unions, the local educational bureau, schools and other educational institutions, focused promotion of
the show as a point of interest to trade unions, study tour groups and senior citizen groups, and
offering group bulk purchase deals to these types of group customers; (ii) also in respect of Moonlight
over Mount Wuyi, updating of marketing slogans, emphasising its key selling points of its water
curtain stage and related stage effects, as well as its cultural educational values, which differentiates
it from other live performances; (iii) in respect of our Chatang hotel, offering bulk purchase discount
for hot bath passes and launching seasonal hot bath passes; (iv) cooperating with various third party
tourism platforms and local hotels to offer promotional deals or sales packages together with other
tourist spots within Mount Wuyi City; (v) in light of a series of large-scale events to take place in
Mount Wuyi City, such as the Cross-Strait Tea Expo (海峽兩岸茶博會), Mount Wuyi International
Marathon (武夷山國際馬拉松), offering specific promotional deals to organisers and participants of
these events alike; (vi) strengthening liaison and cooperation with tour group operators who
specifically arrange self-driving road trip tour groups to broaden our customer base; (vii) increasing
marketing and ads at offline channels, such as at airports, high-speed rail stations, highways; (viii)
increasing online presence marketing, such as setting up official accounts, engaging key opinion
leaders for marketing purpose, and posting on various online video-streaming and content sharing
platforms.
REVIEW OF HISTORICAL RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Year Ended 31 December 2023 Compared to Year Ended 31 December 2022
Revenue
Our revenue increased by approximately RMB80.9 million, or 128.4%, from approximately
RMB63.0 million for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB143.9 million for the
year ended 31 December 2023, primarily attributable to the end of the COVID-19 pandemic which had
led to a resurgence in the regional tourism industry, resulting in a booming tourism sector in Mount
Wuyi during the year. The increase in our revenue in 2023 as compared to 2022 by business segment
is analysed as follows:
(i) The revenue from our shows and performance services increased by approximately
RMB78.5 million, or 135.6% from approximately RMB57.9 million for the year ended 31
December 2022 to approximately RMB136.4 million for the year ended 31 December 2023,
primarily attributable to an increase in the number of performances of our show, Impression
— Dahongpao Scenery Show during the year, as a result of the post-pandemic resurgence
of local tourism industry.
(ii) The revenue from our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business increased by
approximately RMB0.6 million, or 20.0% from approximately RMB3.0 million for the year
ended 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB3.6 million for the year ended 31
December 2023, primarily attributable to the surge in number of tourists as a result of the
post-pandemic resurgence of local tourism industry, which led to increased fixed lease
income from letting out of shop premises.
− 337 −

=== PAGE 346 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
(iii) The revenue from our Chatang hotel business increased by approximately RMB1.8 million,
or 85.7% from approximately RMB2.1 million for the year ended 31 December 2022 to
approximately RMB3.9 million for the year ended 31 December 2023, attributable to an
improvement of its guest room occupancy rate due to the post-pandemic resurgence of the
regional tourism industry as elaborated above.
Cost of Sales
Cost of sales increased by approximately RMB14.9 million, or 32.5% from approximately
RMB45.9 million for the year ended 31 December 2022, to approximately RMB60.8 million for the
year ended 31 December 2023. Such an increase was primarily attributable to an increase in the
number of performances of our show during the year, resulting in an increase in labour costs,
directorial royalty service fees, and costume cleaning and venue cleaning expenses.
Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit increased by approximately RMB65.9 million, or
383.1% from approximately RMB17.2 million for the year ended 31 December 2022, to approximately
RMB83.1 million for the year ended 31 December 2023.
Gross profit margin increased by approximately 30.6 percentage points, from approximately
27.2% for the year ended 31 December 2022, to approximately 57.8% for the year ended 31 December
2023. Such an increase was mainly due to resurgence of the regional tourism industry after COVID-19
restrictions have been lifted. This contributed to a jump in ticket sales from our signature Impression
— Dahongpao Scenery Show, while its cost of sales grew at a slower pace. As a result of the tourism
boost, popularity of the Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show also brought knock-on effects that
contributed to improved results for our Impression Cultural Tourism Town and Chatang hotel.
The gross profit/(loss) and gross profit/(loss) margins by business segment are analysed as
follows:
(i) Shows and performance services
Gross profit for our shows and performance services increased by approximately RMB64.5
million, or 293.2% from approximately RMB22.0 million for the year ended 31 December 2022
to approximately RMB86.5 million for the year ended 31 December 2023, generally in line with
the increased engagement level of our show in Mount Wuyi as a result of the resurgence in the
regional tourism industry during the year. Gross profit margin increased from approximately
38.0% for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately 63.4% for the year ended 31
December 2023, primarily due to the substantial increase in revenue from ticket sales of our
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show outpaced the increase in its cost of sales. Such increase
in cost of sales included renovation expenses and bonus of our employees and salaries of
part-time performance team members as a result of the increase in number of shows performed,
as elaborated in “— Gross profit of our shows and performance services” above.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
(ii) Impression Cultural Tourism Town business
Gross profit for our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business increased by
approximately RMB0.4 million, or 23.5% from approximately RMB1.7 million for the year
ended 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB2.1 million for the year ended 31 December
2023, which was propelled by the resurgence in the regional tourism industry resulting in an
increase in tourist numbers during the year. Gross profit margin increased from approximately
55.6% for the year ended 31 December 2022 to approximately 59.1% for the year ended 31
December 2023, primarily due to an increase in fixed lease income from letting out of shop
premises, while the cost of sales remained stable as fixed cost due to depreciation of land use
rights accounted for a large proportion.
(iii) Chatang hotel business
Gross loss for our Chatang hotel business decreased by approximately RMB1.0 million or

travellers to Mount Wuyi, which directly led to improved guest room occupancy rate of our
Chatang hotel. Gross loss margin decreased from approximately from 313.7% for the year ended
31 December 2022 to approximately 140.9% for the year ended 31 December 2023, due to the
improved results of operation of our Chatang hotel as a result of the resurgence of regional
tourism industry while its cost of sales remained stable.

disposal of financial assets at FVTPL, an increase in our rental income, an increase in bank interest

marketing expenses during the year.
Administrative and Other Operating Expenses

RMB10.4 million for the year ended 31 December 2023, primarily because we incurred more general
property, maintenance expenses, and also recorded an increase in employee related expenses,
primarily because more staff bonus was paid as a result of overall improvement in earnings of our
Group.

Year Ended 31 December 2024 Compared to Year Ended 31 December 2023
Revenue
Our revenue decreased by approximately RMB6.7 million, or 4.7%, from approximately
RMB143.9 million for the year ended 31 December 2023, to approximately RMB137.2 million for the
year ended 31 December 2024, primarily because the driving force of the local tourism sector to the
tourist spending was not as significant as that of in the same period of 2023 despite the fact that our
business operation was still benefited from the post-pandemic resurgence in the tourism industry. The
decrease in our revenue for the year ended 31 December 2024 compared to the year ended 31
December 2023 by business segment is analysed as follows:
(i) The revenue from our shows and performance services decreased by approximately
RMB6.4 million, or 4.7% from approximately RMB 136.4 million for the year ended 31
December 2023 to approximately RMB130.0 million for the year ended 31 December 2024,
primarily attributable to a decrease in the number of tourists who visited Mount Wuyi
bought tickets to watch our signature show. 2023 was a special year which saw strong
rebound in consumer travel spending within the tourism industry following COVID-19.The
boost in 2023 could be attributed to several factors, including the lifting of travel
restrictions, growing consumer confidence, and a strong desire among people to make up
− 340 −

=== PAGE 349 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
for lost travel opportunities during the pandemic, which reflected the release of pent-up
demand for tourism that had been suppressed during the lockdown. As a result, 2023 saw
a significant uptick in tourist activity and spending, highlighting the recovery of the
tourism industry and people’s renewed enthusiasm for travelling. 2023 is generally
perceived as a special year of rapid increase in rebound travels and non-essential
spendings, including leisure spending such as spendings in tourism sector. Comparatively,
the overall performance of the tourism industry in 2024 was relatively stable. This was
because after a period of release of pent-up spending, most people returned to a more
prudent spending mindset. Nonetheless, based on the traveller-to-audience conversion rate
(at 6.7% as recorded in 2023), our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show was
well-received by the audience and had a stable and strong market response. The growth
pattern of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show has shifted toward steady stable
growth instead of rapid growth. Such shift of the growth pattern suggests that it is moving
towards a phase of maturation in its development. Therefore, the decrease in revenue from
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show does not necessarily mean it will become less
attractive going forward. Additionally, such decrease in revenue was partially attributable
to the longer closure of our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show business during the
period between the start of the new year and the start of the Spring Festival (Chinese Lunar
NewYear) holidays, which is the typical rest period for our performers. In 2024, we closed
for 35 days as the Spring Festival occurred in February 2024, compared to our closure for
22 days in 2023 as the Spring Festival occurred in January 2023. Moreover, bad weather
conditions in June 2024 resulted in a drop in audience and even temporary closure of our
performance stage and auditorium for our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show.As the
result of the foregoing, our revenue from the shows and performance services decreased by
approximately RMB6.4 million in 2024.
(ii) The revenue from our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business decreased by RMB0.2
million, or 5.6% from approximately RMB3.6 million for the year ended 31 December 2023
to approximately RMB3.4 million for the year ended 31 December 2024, primarily due to
stabilisation of tourism demand and more prudent consumer spending habits, after a
particularly strong year in 2023 after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions. This is despite
that we continued to focus our resources and attention on enlarging the portfolio of our
cultural tourism service offerings in our Impression CulturalTourismTown to diversify our
business streams, such as by encouraging a night economy for Mount Wuyi by launching
the Impression Market (印象市集) business in October 2024.
(iii) The revenue from our Chatang hotel business decreased by RMB0.1 million, or 2.6% from
approximately RMB3.9 million for the year ended 31 December 2023 to approximately
RMB3.8 million for the year ended 31 December 2024, primarily due to stabilisation of
tourism demand and more prudent consumer spending habits, after a particularly strong
year in 2023 after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions.

Gross Profit and Gross Profit Margin
As a result of the foregoing, our gross profit decreased by approximately RMB1.7 million, or

approximately 7.1 percentage points, from approximately 49.6% for the six months ended 30 June
2024 to approximately 42.5% for the six months ended 30 June 2025.
The gross profit/(loss) and gross profit/(loss)margin by business segment are analysed as
follows:
(i) Shows and performance services
Despite that the revenue from our Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show and performance
services increased by approximately RMB1.6 million from approximately RMB48.0 million for the
six months ended 30 June 2024 to approximately RMB49.6 million for the six months ended 30 June
2025, we made an upward salary adjustments for our employees in September 2024, leading to an
increase of approximately RMB2.4 million cost of sales which was partially offset by decrease in
repair expenses of approximately RMB355,000 for the six months ended 30 June 2025. Consequently,
the gross profit margin decreased from 58.1% for the six months ended 30 June 2024 to 55.3% for the
six months ended 30 June 2025.
In addition, for the six months ended 30 June 2025, our new show Moonlight over Mount Wuyi,
recorded a gross loss margin of 76.7%. As Moonlight Wuyi was established in September 2024, and
the Moonlight over MountWuyi only commenced performance since May 2025, this business was still
in its start-up stages, therefore the current revenue scale remains insufficient to cover its fixed costs
and amortisation.
(ii) Impression Cultural Tourism Town business
Gross profit for our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business decreased by approximately
RMB33,000, or 4.1%, from approximately RMB805,000 for the six months ended 30 June 2024, to
approximately RMB772,000 for the six months ended 30 June 2025. Gross profit margin decreased
by approximately 7.9 percentage points, from approximately 48.2% for the six months ended 30 June
2024 to approximately 40.3% for the six months ended 30 June 2025, primarily due to the increase
in cost of sales resulting from depreciation of right-of-use assets for the newly leased car park in July
2024 and the depreciation of equipment purchased for the newly launched Impression Market in
October 2024.

Inventories
Inventories represent finished goods, primarily being bottled mineral water and Dahongpao tea.
We distribute these bottled mineral water to our VIP seated audience of our signature show free of
charge and Dahongpao tea is used in connection with our business operations. Back in 2022, our
business operations, particularly the number of performances of our signature show, were restricted
by COVID-19, resulting in a higher inventory level for the year, especially the inventory level of
bottled mineral water. In 2023, due to the resurgence in the regional tourism industry which ultimately
led to an increase in our number of performances of the show, our inventories decreased to a
reasonable level of approximately RMB57,000 as at 31 December 2023 from approximately
RMB133,000 as at 31 December 2022. Inventories further decreased from approximately RMB57,000
as at 31 December 2023 to approximately RMB47,000 as at 31 December 2024, attributable to an
increase in our consumption of Dahongpao tea, which was used in both performance, and then to
approximately RMB11,000 as at 30 June 2025 mainly of our show and in connection with the
operation of our Wuyi Rock Tea Research Society.

FINANCIAL INFORMATION
For our ticket selling distributors, who are our customers in respect of our Impression —
Dahongpao Scenery Show, and Moonlight over Mount Wuyi we require these distributors to purchase
our show tickets through prepaid deposits. Before engaging a new customer, we assess the customer’s
credit rate and determine the credit limit for the customer. Credit limits granted to our customers are
reviewed periodically by us. We apply the simplified approach to provide the ECL provisions
prescribed by HKFRS 9, which permits the use of lifetime expected credit loss provision for all trade
receivables. To measure the ECL, trade receivables are grouped based on shared credit risk
characteristics and the days past due. Any historical credit rate is adjusted to reflect current and
forward-looking macroeconomic factors affecting a customer’s ability to settle the amount
outstanding.
Financial Assets at FVTPL
Financial assets at FVTPL represent our fixed-term investment in some financial products with
financial institutions. Our financial assets at FVTPL increased by approximately RMB4.6 million
from approximately RMB3.0 million as at 31 December 2022 to approximately RMB7.6 million as at
31 December 2023, primarily because more financial products became due on 31 December 2023. We
redeemed all of our financial products in December 2024 and made investments in other financial
products in January 2025. Therefore our financial assets at FVTPL recorded nil and approximately
RMB15.3 million as at 31 December 2024 and 30 June 2025, respectively.
If we continue to invest in financial products after Listing, we will comply with requirements
under Chapter 14 of the Listing Rules and disclose the details of our investments and other notifiable
transactions to the extent necessary and as appropriate.
With regards to the purchase and redemption of financial products, we have formulated the
investment policy of diversifying risks and generating steady returns on the premise of ensuring the
safety of funds. We mainly purchase and redeem short-term financial products from time to time for
liquidity management purposes. We generally prefer bank-issued financial products with a relatively
low risk level assigned to them by relevant banks and as stipulated in the purchase agreements for
such products. In terms of investing in financial products, our investment strategy is to diversify risks
and generate returns, while ensuring the safety of the funds. Our chief financial officer and finance
department are mainly responsible for making, implementing and supervising our investment
strategies and decisions. We have implemented the following investment policies:
• Our chief financial officer is responsible for the approval of our investments in financial
products through a strict review and decision-making process;
• Our finance department is responsible for the analysis and research of investments in
financial products, as well as the routine management of such investments; and
• Investments in financial products could be made when we have surplus cash that is not
required for our short-term working capital purposes.
− 352 −

=== PAGE 361 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
We have established internal control measures for investing in financial products, including: (i)
evaluating working capital sufficiency for business needs prior to and after investment; (ii) adopting
a prudent approach in selecting and approving financial assets to minimise financial risks; and (iii)
making case-by-case investment decisions based on factors such as the macroeconomic environment,
market conditions, risk control and expected investment outcomes. In relation to the valuation of
financial products, our Directors (i) reviewed the terms and conditions on the investment agreements,
carefully considered all related information and agreed on the valuation approaches adopted and key
assumptions; and (ii) approved the results if the procedures were deemed satisfactory and it was
unnecessary to appoint external valuation expert to conduct the valuation. Based on the above
processes, our Directors are of the view that the valuation analysis is fair and reasonable, and the fair
value measurements of financial products are properly prepared.

QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURE ABOUT MARKET RISKS
We are exposed to various types of financial and market risks, including foreign currency risk,
interest rate risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. Our operation management is responsible for the risk
management. For details, see note 32 to the Accountants’ Report included in Appendix I to this
prospectus.
Foreign currency risk
Foreign currency risk refers to the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial
instrument will fluctuate because of changes in foreign exchange rates. Our Group and our Company’s
business mainly operates in China with most of its transactions denominated and settled in RMB and
therefore exposure to foreign currency translation risk is considered not significant. Our Group and
our Company had not used any financial instrument to hedge against foreign exchange risk.
Interest rate risk
Interest rate risk relates to the risk that the fair value or cash flows of a financial instrument will
fluctuate because of changes in market interest rates. Lease liabilities bearing fixed rates expose our
Group and our Company to fair value interest rate risk. Our Group’s and our Company’s bank balances
are mainly pay variable interest rates.
Credit risk
Credit risk refers to the risk that the counterparty to a financial instrument would fail to
discharge its obligation under the terms of the financial instrument and cause a financial loss to our
Group. Our Group’s exposure to credit risk mainly arises from granting credit to customers in the
ordinary course of its operations. Our Group’s maximum exposure to credit risk is limited to the
carrying amounts of the financial assets at the end of each reporting period as detailed in note 32.1
to the Accountants’ Report included in Appendix I to this prospectus.
Liquidity Risk
Liquidity risk relates to the risk that our Group will not be able to meet its obligations associated
with its financial liabilities that are settled by delivering cash or another financial asset. Our Group
is exposed to liquidity risk in respect of settlement of its payables, and also in respect of its cash flow
management. Our Group’s objective is to maintain an appropriate level of liquid assets and committed
lines of funding to meet its liquidity requirements in the short and longer term.
DIVIDENDS
In May 2024, we fully paid dividends of RMB32.4 million. We declared dividends of RMB41.1
million in March 2025, which was settled on 22 April 2025.
Our Board is responsible for submitting proposals in respect of dividend payments, if any, to the
Shareholders’ general meeting for approval. Our Board may declare dividends in the future after
taking into account our distributable profits, financial condition, cash flows, expected future capital
− 365 −

=== PAGE 374 ===
FINANCIAL INFORMATION
expenditure, return to our Shareholders, capital requirements, finance costs, the external financing
environment and any other factors that the Directors may deem relevant. Any declaration and
payment, as well as the amount of, dividends will be subject to the requirements of our Article of
Association, the PRC Company Law and the NEEQ rules and regulations. Under the PRC Company
Law and our Articles of Association, dividends are distributed to our Shareholders in proportion to
their shareholdings. We currently do not have any fixed pay-out ratio for future cash dividends. The
payment of dividends may also be limited by legal restrictions.
In any event, we will pay dividends out of our profit after tax only after we have made the
following allocations:
(a) recovery of accumulated losses, if any;
(b) allocation to the statutory common reserve fund an amount of 10% of our profit after tax,
as determined under theAccounting Standards for Business Enterprises issued by the MOF
(the “PRC GAAP”); until such fund has reached more than 50% of our registered capital;
and
(c) allocation, if any, to a discretionary common reserve fund an amount approved by the
Shareholders in a Shareholders’ meeting.
Payment of dividends is also subject to restrictions under PRC laws. Under PRC laws, dividends
may be paid only out of distributable profits. Distributable profits are our net profit as determined
under PRC GAAP, less any recovery of accumulated losses and appropriations to statutory and other
reserves that we are required to make.

(1) approximately HK$25.4 million (equivalent to approximately RMB23.2 million),

a premium platform for exploring the Mount Wuyi Dahongpao tea culture. We will
gradually complete updates of our signature show during the off-season and
non-performance periods, ensuring that the updates do not cause any interruptions to the
performances of our show.

(2) approximately HK$31.6 million (equivalent to approximately RMB28.7 million),

and landscaping that reflect the natural beauty of the area.Additionally, we aim to upgrade

道). It is located in our Impression Cultural Tourism Town and is located next to the

featuring a traditional Chinese garden design.This multifunctional facilities in the museum
integrates display, appreciation, experience and education, offering a comprehensive
exhibition space that fully showcases and reflects the tea culture of Mount Wuyi.
The launch of our Impression Cultural Tourism Town offers a transformative travelling
experience for travellers to Mount Wuyi, presenting an enriched and varied selection of
leisure and travel activities. This initiative not only encourages tourists to prolong their
visits but also allows them to explore Mount Wuyi’s rich history and dynamic culture more
deeply. Our Directors are of the view that our Impression Cultural Tourism Town is more
than a mere tourist spot; and strategically, it plays a crucial role in bolstering MountWuyi’s
night economy. By enhancing the local cultural and tourism offerings, the town stimulates
growth in related industries, such as dining and accommodation, ultimately generating job
opportunities for local residents.Although our Impression Cultural Tourism Town business
did not contribute a significant portion of revenue to the total revenue of our Group during
the Track Record Period, its strategic importance to the local tourism economy is
undeniable. Therefore, the expansion of our Impression Cultural Tourism Town extends its
strategic effects on both our Group and the tourism industry of Mount Wuyi. See “Business
— Impression Cultural Tourism Town Business — Strategic Importance of our Impression
Cultural Tourism Town” in this prospectus for a detailed illustration.

withstanding the challenges posed by the shows performed by our competitors in the

Identifying and Acquiring Quality Project
We will conduct rigorous due diligence on target projects based in the established target
markets and apply our selection criteria to ensure that selected project meet the following
standards:
• Preliminary Screening: We will conduct an initial assessment of the potential project
based on the target market directions and specific criteria to determine if we should
advance to the next stage for in-depth investigation.
• Due Diligence: We will conduct comprehensive legal, financial, and technical due
diligence on the potential project to ensure that the information is accurate and
reliable.
• Comprehensive Evaluation: We will invite external consultants and internal experts
to assemble an evaluation committee to comprehensively evaluate the target project
and select the best cooperation partner.
• Key Metrics: Our target tourism performance project shall be able to attract
approximately 150,000 audience and is projected to generate revenue of
approximately RMB15.0 million on an annual basis.
Through these measures, we will ensure that our proceeds are allocated effectively to the
most promising cultural tourism performance project. According to Frost & Sullivan, there
were approximately 17,781 national art performance organisations, of which 486 are
located in Fujian Province at the end of 2024. Additionally, the box office receipts of live
performances in Fujian Province reached approximately RMB1.79 billion. As at the Latest
Practicable Date, we had identified two potential targets primarily in Fujian Province, but
we had not entered into, nor have we proposed to enter into, any letter of intent,
memorandum of understanding or agreement with respect to acquisition of any potential
targets. One of the targets focuses on the cultural connotations and performance of a
Chinese legend, incorporating classic legends and cultural elements to enhance artistic
impact and cultural dissemination value. The other target focuses on the performance of
historical stories and folk customs of Fuzhou City by virtue of virtual reality and
augmented reality technologies to provide an immersive viewing experience.
We expect that the net proceeds allocated to the said acquisition will be fully utilised by
2027, on the basis that the broader cultural tourism market can be substantially recovered
from the post-pandemic effects, also prerequisite on our management assessment followed
with a conclusion that the risk associated to the acquisition is minimised to the extent
reasonable.

(4) approximately HK$12.1 million (equivalent to approximately RMB11.1 million),
representing approximately 11.0% of the net proceeds from the Global Offering, will be
used for promotional efforts to enhance our brand image and increase our business
presence, focusing on elevating the visibility of our upgraded signature show, our new
show, i.e., Moonlight over Mount Wuyi, Impression Cultural Tourism Town and Chatang
hotel.
A summary of our promotional strategies with justifications is set out below.
(i) Digital Marketing and Social Media Promotion
We believe in the prevalent digital landscape, platforms such as Weibo, Douyin and
Xiaohongshu are essential for attracting younger audience and potential tourists. By
creating official accounts and sharing high-quality contents such as performance
previews, behind-the-scenes footage, performer interviews and highlights, our
brand’s visibility can steadily improve. Collaborating with influencers and hosting
online interactive events can quickly expand reach and engage more followers.
(ii) Content Marketing and Cultural Dissemination
Leveraging Mount Wuyi’s rich cultural heritage, a series of culturally engaging
marketing contents can be created, including documentaries, short videos and
illustrated stories that explore Dahongpao tea culture and local traditions of
UNESCO-recognised Mount Wuyi. This approach not only cultivates the public in
line with the roll-out of concepts of “music + tourism”, “performance + tourism”,
“sports + tourism” and other innovative performance formats underlined by the
Measures for Creating New Consumption Scenarios and Fostering New Growth Points
in Consumption 《( 關於打造消費新場景培育消費新增長點的措施》), but also
enhances our brand’s appeal. Such marketing contents can be shared on the official
website, video platforms and social media, generating positive word-of-mouth
referrals.
(iii) Offline Events and Experiential Marketing
We also consider organising a variety of offline activities such as cultural festivals,
art exhibitions and outdoor concerts, inviting local residents and travellers to
participate and fostering a vibrant cultural atmosphere. Specially designed
family-friendly activities such as tea leaf crafting and traditional skill workshops,
allow travellers to experience the charm of Mount Wuyi firsthand. Thoughtful event
setups and interactive elements can seamlessly integrate brand messaging, enhancing
travellers’ recognition of our brand. This promotional strategy also aligns with our
strategic importance of expanding our Impression Cultural Tourism Town Business.

(iv) Media Public Relations and News Releases
We will also hold press conferences or media briefings to update the public on our
project developments, important events, and future plans, maintaining strong media

highlight innovative initiatives and social responsibility efforts, helping to establish
a positive corporate image. Moreover, we will participate in industry forums and
seminars to showcase our expertise and leadership in the broader cultural tourism
industry.

(5) approximately HK$8.2 million (equivalent to approximately RMB7.4 million),
representing approximately 7.4% of the net proceeds from the Global Offering, will be used
for upgrade of our ticket management system and software, with objectives to (i) achieve
seamless integration of service offerings and operating data across our business segments;
(ii) implement real-time monitoring across our business segments, ensuring unified data
presentation; (iii) substantiate data-drive management and marketing; and (iv) utilise
operating data and utilise the same to provide insights for management decisions. In
particular, we will upgrade our ticket management system and our ticket selling distributor
management system. Specifically, our updated ticket management system will cover a
marketing mini-program for media liaison such that we will become able to communicate
with external parties for marketing purpose. Our upgraded ticket selling distributor
management system will cover the management of the ticket selling distributors of both
Impression — Dahongpao Scenery Show and Moonlight over Mount Wuyi, covering the
records of credit scores and performance of each of our ticket selling distributors.
Additionally, the updated ticket selling distributor management system will be able to
record all the details of authorised agents of our ticket selling distributors such that we can
communicate with these authorised agents to better grasp the onward ticket sales activities.
Also, we will develop an integrated mobile application that integrates all of our cultural
tourism service offerings, featuring multiple functions including one-stop ticket
purchasing, real-time information access, personalised itinerary recommendations for
travellers, online customer support and tourist reviews. Our Directors are of the view that
our targeted upgrade of our ticket management system and software can streamline,
standardise and enhance the transparency of operating process, thereby improving our
operating efficiency and enhancing tourist experience and satisfaction.
We expect that the net proceeds allocated to our upgrade of ticket management system and
software will be fully utilised by 2027.

representing approximately 10.0% of the net proceeds from the Global Offering, will be

ACTIVITIES BY SYNDICATE MEMBERS
We describe below a variety of activities that underwriters of the Hong Kong Public Offering and
the International Offering (together referred to as “Syndicate Members”), may each individually

The Syndicate Members and their affiliates are diversified financial institutions with
relationships in countries around the world. These entities engage in a wide range of commercial and
investment banking, brokerage, funds management, trading, hedging, investing and other activities for
their own account and for the accounts of others. In the ordinary course of their various business
activities, the Syndicate Members and their respective affiliates may purchase, sell or hold a broad
array of investments and actively trade securities, derivatives, loans, commodities, currencies, credit
default swaps and other financial instruments for their own account and for the accounts of their
customers. Such investment and trading activities may involve or relate to assets, securities and/or
instruments of our Company and/or persons and entities with relationships with our Company and may
also include swaps and other financial instruments entered into for hedging purposes in connection
with the Group’s loans and other debt.
In relation to our H Shares, those activities could include acting as agent for buyers and sellers
of the H Shares, entering into transactions with those buyers and sellers in a principal capacity,
proprietary trading in the H Shares, and entering into over the counter or listed derivative transactions
or listed or unlisted securities transactions (including issuing securities such derivative warrants listed
on a stock exchange) which have as their underlying assets, assets including the H Shares. Those
activities may require hedging activity by those entities involving, directly or indirectly, the buying

Allocation
Allocation of the Offer Shares to investors under the Hong Kong Public Offering will be based
solely on the level of valid applications received under the Hong Kong Public Offering. The basis of
allocation may vary, depending on the number of Hong Kong Offer Shares validly applied for by
applicants. Such allocation could, where appropriate, consist of balloting, which could mean that
some applicants may receive a higher allocation than others who have applied for the same number
of Hong Kong Offer Shares, and those applicants who are not successful in the ballot may not receive
any Hong Kong Offer Shares.
For allocation purposes only, the total number of Hong Kong Offer Shares available under the
Hong Kong Public Offering (after taking into account any reallocation referred to below) will be
divided equally (to the nearest board lot) into two pools: pool A and pool B, with any odd board lots
being allocated to pool A. Accordingly, the maximum number of Hong Kong Offer Shares initially in
poolAand pool B will be 1,805,000 and 1,805,000, respectively.The Hong Kong Offer Shares in pool
A will be allocated on an equitable basis to applicants who have applied for Hong Kong Offer Shares
with an aggregate subscription price of HK$5 million (excluding the brokerage, SFC transaction levy,
AFRC transaction levy and Stock Exchange trading fee payable) or less. The Hong Kong Offer Shares
in pool B will be allocated on an equitable basis to applicants who have applied for Hong Kong Offer
Shares with an aggregate subscription price of more than HK$5 million (excluding the brokerage, SFC
transaction levy, AFRC transaction levy and Stock Exchange trading fee payable) and up to the total
value in pool B.

different allocation ratios. If any Hong Kong Offer Shares in one (but not both) of the pools are

demand in that other pool and be allocated accordingly. For the purpose of this paragraph only, the
“price” for the Offer Shares means the price payable on application therein (without regard to the
Offer Price as finally determined). Applicants can only receive an allocation of the Hong Kong Offer
